You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.text:
Jonathan,

I reviewed the initial draft SPA that Douglas Renwick at Fortuna & Blake circulated yesterday. My overall impression: this is a heavily seller-favorable draft in several material respects, and some of the positions directly contradict the September 10 term sheet — which tells me either Doug is testing our resolve or his client gave him different instructions than what was agreed at the principal level. Either way, we need a sharp, comprehensive markup.

Marcus Devereaux at Whitmore Capital wants to see our redline by end of next week. Given the November 14 target signing date, that gives the parties roughly two weeks of negotiation runway after we send our markup, which is tight. I need your comprehensive markup memorandum with redlined provisions and full track-changes commentary.

**General Instructions**

Cross-reference every material provision against three sources: (1) the executed term sheet dated September 10, 2025, (2) the firm's M&A Playbook for environmental services sector acquisitions, and (3) the environmental due diligence summary memo prepared by our environmental group.

For each issue you identify, I need you to:

(a) Quote the original Seller's draft language;
(b) Provide proposed revised language in full — actual contract text, not summaries;
(c) Include a brief track-changes comment explaining the legal or commercial rationale and citing the relevant source document (term sheet, playbook, or DD memo); and
(d) Assign a priority level: Critical, High, or Medium.

Draft real contract language. Doug Renwick is a sharp practitioner and we need our markup to be precise — no placeholders or brackets where we can avoid them.

Organize the memorandum by SPA article/section for easy navigation.

---

**PRIORITY ISSUES**

**1. MAE Definition — CRITICAL**

This is at the top of my list. The Seller's draft carves out changes affecting "the environmental services industry generally" and "changes in environmental laws or regulations" from the MAE definition. The problem is obvious: Cascadia Environmental Solutions *is* an environmental services company. If the entire environmental services industry suffers a downturn, or if a major regulatory change fundamentally alters compliance economics, those are precisely the risks that should constitute an MAE for this target. As drafted, these carve-outs effectively gut the MAE closing condition.

Add a "disproportionate impact" qualifier to both carve-outs, consistent with the playbook position. The exception should read along the lines of: "except to the extent such changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the environmental services industry." This is non-negotiable from Whitmore's perspective.

**2. Sandbagging Provision (Section 9.06) — CRITICAL**

I noticed an express anti-sandbagging provision in Section 9.06 — the draft says Buyer cannot recover for any breach of which Buyer "had Knowledge as of the Closing Date." This is a dealbreaker.

The playbook mandates a pro-sandbagging clause in every PE acquisition, and for good reason. Whitmore has conducted extensive diligence and has identified various issues — including the Dalton Creek CERCLA matter — and they cannot afford to have their indemnification rights cut off by virtue of having done thorough diligence. The whole point of representations and warranties is allocation of risk regardless of Buyer's knowledge.

Replace the anti-sandbagging language with an affirmative pro-sandbagging provision stating that Buyer's right to indemnification is not limited or affected by any knowledge obtained by Buyer or its representatives at any time, whether before or after Closing, regardless of whether such knowledge relates to a breach. Draft this tightly.

**3. Earnout Operational Covenants (Section 2.05) — CRITICAL**

The earnout provision is a major concern. The Seller's draft includes language requiring Buyer to operate the Target's business "in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment." This is an extremely aggressive seller position. It would effectively give Seller veto power over Buyer's integration plans during the earnout period through December 31, 2026.

Whitmore is acquiring Cascadia as a platform investment — they intend to make operational improvements, potentially acquire bolt-on targets, and restructure the business. An affirmative covenant to "maximize" the earnout would create litigation risk on virtually any business decision.

Per the playbook, the only acceptable earnout covenant is a negative covenant: Buyer shall not take actions with the *primary purpose* of avoiding or reducing the earnout payment. No affirmative operational obligations. Revise accordingly.

Also confirm the earnout financial mechanics match the term sheet: $25,000,000 maximum earnout payment; $38,000,000 Adjusted EBITDA threshold for full payment; $32,000,000 floor for pro-rata payment; linear interpolation between $32M and $38M (approximately $4,166,667 per $1,000,000 of EBITDA above $32,000,000); measurement period ending December 31, 2026. Flag any discrepancies.

**4. Government Contract Consents — CRITICAL**

I reviewed the environmental DD memo and the government contract issue is not addressed anywhere in the Seller's draft conditions to closing. Cascadia holds 4 active government contracts — Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, US Army Corps of Engineers, and Bureau of Land Management.

While this is a stock deal and the contracting entity (Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.) does not technically change, the federal Anti-Assignment Act (41 U.S.C. § 6305) and FAR 42.12 require novation agreements when a government contractor undergoes a change in ownership or control. A stock acquisition resulting in a new parent entity generally triggers the novation requirement under FAR 42.1204. Failure to obtain novation or recognition agreements could give the government the right to terminate the contracts.

These contracts are likely material to the Target's revenue and backlog. Add: (a) a pre-closing covenant requiring Seller and the Company to cooperate in filing novation/recognition requests with the relevant agencies; (b) representations regarding the government contracts and their assignment/novation requirements; and (c) consider whether government contract novation should be a closing condition or a pre-/post-closing covenant. Making it a hard closing condition is likely impractical given agency timelines, so a covenant with cooperation obligations and reasonable best efforts may be more appropriate — but flag this for discussion with the client. I plan to raise the timing question with Marcus on Monday.

---

**ADDITIONAL ISSUES**

**5. Indemnification Cap (Indemnification Article) — HIGH**

The indemnification article needs a hard scrub against the term sheet. I noticed the general indemnification cap appears to be set at 20% of enterprise value ($43,000,000), but the term sheet clearly provides for a 12.5% cap ($26,875,000). This is not a drafting gray area — the term sheet is unambiguous. Redline this to 12.5% and include a comment citing the applicable section of the term sheet.

Also confirm the escrow mechanics: $16,125,000 (7.5% of the $215,000,000 enterprise value) held with Pinnacle Trust Company, 18 months for general claims and 36 months for Fundamental Reps and Special Indemnities.

**6. Environmental Rep Survival Period — HIGH**

The DD memo from the environmental group flagged the Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure (potential liability of $1,500,000 to $6,000,000) and the active Hargrove Industrial Site remediation ($4,200,000 remaining costs). A 12-month survival period for environmental reps is wholly inadequate for an environmental services company. Extend environmental rep survival to a minimum of 36 months per the playbook, and flag the option of seeking the full statute of limitations period — noting that CERCLA has no statute of limitations for government cost recovery actions. I want to discuss with Marcus whether to push for the longer period.

**7. Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek — HIGH**

Tied to the environmental survival issue. The term sheet specifically provides for a "Special Indemnity" for the Dalton Creek disposal facility matter. The Seller's draft does not include any special indemnity — it treats Dalton Creek as a general rep matter only.

Draft a Special Indemnity provision: 72-month survival, not subject to the basket or general cap, with the escrow holdback available for 36 months for Special Indemnity claims. The provision should cover all losses arising from or relating to the Dalton Creek disposal facility, including the pending EPA information request under CERCLA § 104(e) and any resulting investigation, cleanup, or enforcement action.

**8. Interim Covenant — Affiliate Transactions — HIGH**

The interim operating covenants section is missing any restriction on affiliate transactions between Seller and the Company. Remember that the EBITDA adjustments include $1,600,000 of above-market rent paid by Cascadia to a Seller affiliate. Without a covenant restricting affiliate dealings during the interim period, Seller could expand those arrangements or enter into new ones. The playbook is clear: require Buyer's prior written consent for any new, amended, or terminated transaction with Seller or Seller affiliates. Add this covenant.

**9. Debt Payoff Mechanics — HIGH**

The Seller's draft is vague on closing indebtedness repayment — it says indebtedness will be repaid "on or promptly following the Closing Date." This doesn't work for Whitmore or for Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp. (the $125M acquisition lender). The term sheet requires payoff letters from all holders of Target indebtedness — Cascade Mutual Bank ($28,000,000 senior term loan), Pacific Lease Corp. ($9,800,000 equipment financing), and the $4,500,000 subordinated seller note from Evergreen Holdings — at least 3 business days prior to closing, with wire instructions. All indebtedness must be repaid simultaneously at closing through the funds flow. Add payoff letter delivery as a closing condition and revise the payment mechanics accordingly.

**10. Environmental Permit Transfer Cooperation — MEDIUM**

The DD memo identified that many state environmental permits in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada require notification to or approval from the issuing agency upon a change of control, even in a stock deal where the permit-holding entity remains the same legal entity. Target holds 23 active environmental permits. The Seller's draft includes a representation that Target holds all required permits but has no pre-closing or post-closing cooperation covenant for permit transfers or notifications.

Add a cooperation covenant requiring Seller to assist with permit transfer notifications and applications both before and after closing. Even in a stock transaction, state regulators often treat a change of ultimate beneficial ownership as a trigger for notification. Oregon DEQ and Washington Ecology both have these requirements.

**11. R&W Insurance Subrogation Waiver — MEDIUM**

Whitmore Capital is obtaining a representations and warranties insurance policy from Granite Ridge Underwriters. The term sheet acknowledges this and the playbook requires that the SPA include a waiver of the insurer's subrogation rights against Seller except in cases of fraud. The Seller's draft makes no mention of R&W Insurance at all.

Add a provision in the miscellaneous article (or indemnification article) providing that any R&W Insurance policy obtained by Buyer or its affiliates shall not provide the insurer with any subrogation rights against Seller or its affiliates, except in cases of Seller's fraud. This is standard in the current market and Seller's counsel should expect it.

**12. Non-Competition Covenant Scope — MEDIUM**

The non-compete in the Seller's draft is far too broad — 5 years, all of the United States, "any business." The term sheet is explicit: 3 years post-closing, limited to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services, in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada only. Evergreen Holdings Group has construction and timber operations that would be swept in by the overbroad language, which is both commercially unreasonable and raises enforceability concerns under applicable state law. Narrow to match the term sheet exactly.

---

**ITEMS THAT ARE FINE AS DRAFTED — DO NOT MARK UP**

A few things I reviewed that I think are fine as drafted — don't waste time marking these up:

- The indemnification basket at 1% of enterprise value ($2,150,000) as a true deductible is within the playbook range of 0.75%–1.0% for a deal of this size. Leave it.
- The Knowledge qualifier (actual knowledge of Patricia Huang and Robert Merrill, no constructive knowledge) is acceptable per the playbook for targets with fewer than 500 employees. Cascadia has 340 employees. Leave it.
- Good standing certificate delivery within 10 days of closing is standard (playbook says 5–10 business days). Leave it.
- Delaware governing law is appropriate — both Buyer and Seller are Delaware entities. Leave it.

Focus your energy on the real issues. If you spot anything else that seems off but isn't on my list above, flag it in a separate section at the end of your memo so we can discuss.

---

**TIMING AND NEXT STEPS**

I need the markup memorandum from you by COB Wednesday, October 29. I want to review it Thursday morning and send the redline to Douglas Renwick at Fortuna & Blake by Friday, October 31, so the parties can schedule a negotiation call the following week.

Coordinate with the environmental group if you have questions on the DD memo findings — particularly regarding the Dalton Creek liability estimates and the permit transfer requirements.

I have a call with Marcus Devereaux on Monday, October 27, and I will raise the government contract novation timing issue (closing condition vs. covenant) and the environmental rep survival period question (36 months vs. full statute of limitations). For now, draft your markup assuming 36 months for environmental rep survival but flag the longer alternative so we can pivot if Marcus wants to push harder.

If anything in the draft raises a question that requires client input before you can finalize a position, loop me in right away — don't hold the memo for it.

You should already have all the key documents in the deal folder on the document management system: the Seller's initial draft SPA (sellers-draft-spa.docx) circulated by Renwick on October 22; the executed term sheet dated September 10, 2025 (executed-term-sheet.docx); the firm's M&A Playbook for environmental services sector acquisitions (buyer-ma-playbook.docx); and the environmental due diligence summary memo (environmental-dd-memo.docx). If anything is missing, let me know.

Thanks, Jonathan. Let me know if you have questions before you dive in.

Best,

Elena Vasquez-Moreno
Partner
Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP
71 South Wacker Drive, Suite 4500
Chicago, IL 60606
evasquez-moreno@apylaw.com

1: **BINDING TERM SHEET**
2: 
3: **Acquisition of 100% of the Outstanding Equity Interests of** **Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**
4: 
5: Dated as of September 10, 2025
6: 
7: This Binding Term Sheet (this \"Term Sheet\") sets forth the principal terms and conditions agreed upon by the parties identified below with respect to the proposed acquisition described herein. Except as set forth in Section 18 (Binding Provisions) below, this Term Sheet is intended to be binding on the parties and shall govern the preparation of the Definitive Agreement (as defined below). This Term Sheet supersedes and replaces in its entirety the non-binding Letter of Intent dated August 15, 2025 (the \"LOI\"), previously entered into between Whitmore Capital Partners LLC and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. with respect to the proposed acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the context in which they appear.
8: 
9: **[Section 1: Parties]{.underline}**
10: 
11: **Buyer:** Whitmore Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, with its principal offices at 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 3100, Chicago, Illinois 60606 (referred to herein as \"Buyer\" or \"Whitmore\").
12: 
13: **Seller:** Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices at 1550 NW Everett Street, Suite 800, Portland, Oregon 97209 (referred to herein as \"Seller\" or \"Evergreen\").
14: 
15: **Target / the Company:** Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc., an Oregon corporation, with its principal offices at 8700 SW Tualatin-Sherwood Road, Suite 200, Tualatin, Oregon 97062 (referred to herein as \"Target,\" \"Cascadia,\" or the \"Company\").
16: 
17: Seller is the sole stockholder of Target, holding one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Target, consisting of 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share (the \"Shares\"). No other shares of capital stock or other equity interests of the Company are issued or outstanding as of the date of this Term Sheet.
18: 
19: **[Section 2: Transaction Structure]{.underline}**
20: 
21: **Stock Purchase.** Buyer shall acquire from Seller, and Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, and deliver to Buyer, all 1,000,000 issued and outstanding Shares, representing one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Company. As of the date of this Term Sheet, no options, warrants, convertible securities, or other instruments convertible into or exercisable or exchangeable for equity interests of the Company are outstanding, and Seller shall represent and warrant to such effect in the Definitive Agreement. Following the Closing (as defined below), the Company will be a wholly-owned subsidiary of Buyer.
22: 
23: **Definitive Agreement.** The transaction shall be documented in a definitive Stock Purchase Agreement (the \"Definitive Agreement\" or the \"SPA\"), which shall be prepared in the first instance by Seller\'s counsel, Fortuna & Blake LLP, and delivered to Buyer\'s counsel, Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP, for review and negotiation. The Definitive Agreement shall contain the terms and conditions set forth in this Term Sheet, together with such additional terms and conditions as are customary for transactions of this nature and as may be mutually agreed by the parties. The Definitive Agreement shall be consistent with the terms of this Term Sheet in all material respects. In the event of a conflict between this Term Sheet and the Definitive Agreement, the parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve such conflict; provided, however, that the economic terms set forth herein (including without limitation the Base Enterprise Value, the purchase price formula, the indemnification cap and basket, the Special Indemnity terms, the escrow terms, and the earnout terms) shall control until expressly superseded by a mutually executed Definitive Agreement.
24: 
25: **[Section 3: Purchase Price]{.underline}**
26: 
27: **Base Enterprise Value.** The base enterprise value of the Company for purposes of this transaction shall be Two Hundred Fifteen Million Dollars (\$215,000,000) (the \"Base Enterprise Value\").
28: 
29: **Purchase Price Formula.** The purchase price to be paid by Buyer to Seller for the Shares (the \"Purchase Price\") shall be calculated as follows:
30: 
31: > Purchase Price = Base Enterprise Value + Estimated Closing Net Working Capital -- Estimated Closing Indebtedness -- Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses
32: 
33: **Target Net Working Capital.** The target net working capital for the Company (the \"Target NWC\") shall be Eighteen Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,200,000), calculated in accordance with the methodology to be set forth in the Definitive Agreement and consistent with United States generally accepted accounting principles (\"GAAP\") as historically applied by the Company.
34: 
35: **Estimated Closing Statement.** Seller shall deliver to Buyer a good faith estimated closing statement (the \"Estimated Closing Statement\") setting forth Seller\'s reasonable estimates of (i) Closing Net Working Capital (\"Estimated Closing NWC\"), (ii) Closing Indebtedness (\"Estimated Closing Indebtedness\"), and (iii) Seller Transaction Expenses (\"Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses\"), in each case calculated as of the Closing Date, no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. The Estimated Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with GAAP as historically applied by the Company and in a manner consistent with the methodology to be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
36: 
37: **Illustrative Calculation.** The following calculation is provided for reference purposes only and shall not be deemed to establish the actual Purchase Price or any component thereof:
38: 
39:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

42:   Base Enterprise Value                         \$215,000,000
43:

45:

47: 
48:   Less: Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses   (\$3,900,000)

58: >

60: >

Following the Closing, Buyer shall prepare a final closing statement reflecting the actual Closing NWC, Closing Indebtedness, and Seller Transaction Expenses as of the Closing Date. The post-closing true-up process shall be completed within ninety (90) days following the Closing Date. Standard dispute resolution procedures, including referral to an independent accounting firm mutually acceptable to the parties for resolution of any disputed items, shall be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
72: 
73: **[Section 4: Escrow]{.underline}**
74: 
75: **Escrow Amount.** At the Closing, Buyer shall deposit Sixteen Million One Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$16,125,000) (the \"Escrow Amount\"), which is equal to seven and one-half percent (7.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value (\$215,000,000 × 0.075 = \$16,125,000), with Pinnacle Trust Company, as escrow agent (the \"Escrow Agent\"), pursuant to an escrow agreement in customary form and substance to be agreed upon by the parties and the Escrow Agent (the \"Escrow Agreement\"). The Escrow Amount shall be deducted from the Purchase Price payable to Seller at Closing.
76: 
77: **Escrow Purpose.** The Escrow Amount shall serve as security for Seller\'s indemnification obligations under the Definitive Agreement. The Escrow Amount shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for Buyer\'s indemnification claims with respect to breaches of non-Fundamental Representations, up to the Escrow Amount; provided that claims for Losses exceeding the Escrow Amount (but subject to the Cap set forth in Section 8 below) may be pursued directly against Seller. For the avoidance of doubt, the escrow shall also serve as a source of recovery for claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity as set forth in Section 9 below.
78: 
79: **Escrow Release Schedule.** The Escrow Amount shall be released in accordance with the following schedule:
80: 
81: > \(a\) *General Indemnification Claims (Non-Fundamental Representations):* The portion of the Escrow Amount allocable to general indemnification claims shall be released to Seller on the date that is eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, less any amounts subject to pending and unresolved indemnification claims as of such date.
82: >
83: > \(b\) *Fundamental Representations and Special Indemnities:* The portion of the Escrow Amount allocable to Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be released to Seller on the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, less any amounts subject to pending and unresolved indemnification claims as of such date.
84: 
85: Any portion of the Escrow Amount that is not subject to pending or unresolved indemnification claims as of the applicable release date shall be promptly released to Seller. The specific allocation of the Escrow Amount between general indemnification claims and Fundamental Representations/Special Indemnity claims shall be set forth in the Escrow Agreement.
86: 
87: **[Section 5: Earnout]{.underline}**
88: 
89: **Maximum Earnout Payment.** In addition to the Purchase Price, Buyer shall pay to Seller an earnout payment (the \"Earnout Payment\") of up to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), subject to the terms and conditions set forth below.
90: 
91: **Measurement Period.** The Earnout Payment shall be calculated based on the Company\'s financial performance during the trailing twelve-month (TTM) period ending December 31, 2026 (the \"Measurement Period\").
92: 
93: **Metric.** The Earnout Payment shall be based on the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period. \"Adjusted EBITDA\" shall be calculated in a manner consistent with the Company\'s historical practice and as defined in the Definitive Agreement, and shall exclude the impact of purchase price accounting adjustments, transaction-related costs, integration costs, and any other items mutually agreed to be excluded by the parties as set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
94: 
95: **Threshold and Floor.**
96: 
97: > \(a\) *Full Earnout:* If the Company achieves TTM Adjusted EBITDA of Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000) or more for the Measurement Period, the full Earnout Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) shall be payable to Seller.
98: >
99: > \(b\) *Floor:* No Earnout Payment shall be payable if TTM Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is less than Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000).
100: >
101: > \(c\) *Pro-Rata Calculation:* If TTM Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is equal to or greater than Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), the Earnout Payment shall be calculated on a linear interpolation basis in accordance with the following formula:
102: >
103: > Earnout Payment = (\$25,000,000 / (\$38,000,000 -- \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA -- \$32,000,000)
104: >
105: > which equals approximately \$4,166,667 per \$1,000,000 of Adjusted EBITDA above \$32,000,000.
106:

lines.text: **BINDING TERM SHEET**
**Acquisition of 100% of the Outstanding Equity Interests of** **Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**
Dated as of September 10, 2025

This Binding Term Sheet (this \"Term Sheet\") sets forth the principal terms and conditions agreed upon by the parties identified below with respect to the proposed acquisition described herein. Except as set forth in Section 18 (Binding Provisions) below, this Term Sheet is intended to be binding on the parties and shall govern the preparation of the Definitive Agreement (as defined below). This Term Sheet supersedes and replaces in its entirety the non-binding Letter of Intent dated August 15, 2025 (the \"LOI\"), previously entered into between Whitmore Capital Partners LLC and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. with respect to the proposed acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the context in which they appear.
**[Section 1: Parties]{.underline}**

**Buyer:** Whitmore Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, with its principal offices at 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 3100, Chicago, Illinois 60606 (referred to herein as \"Buyer\" or \"Whitmore\").

**Seller:** Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc., a Delaware corporation, with its principal offices at 1550 NW Everett Street, Suite 800, Portland, Oregon 97209 (referred to herein as \"Seller\" or \"Evergreen\").

**Target / the Company:** Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc., an Oregon corporation, with its principal offices at 8700 SW Tualatin-Sherwood Road, Suite 200, Tualatin, Oregon 97062 (referred to herein as \"Target,\" \"Cascadia,\" or the \"Company\").

Seller is the sole stockholder of Target, holding one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Target, consisting of 1,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share (the \"Shares\"). No other shares of capital stock or other equity interests of the Company are issued or outstanding as of the date of this Term Sheet.
**[Section 2: Transaction Structure]{.underline}**

**Stock Purchase.** Buyer shall acquire from Seller, and Seller shall sell, assign, transfer, and deliver to Buyer, all 1,000,000 issued and outstanding Shares, representing one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding equity interests of the Company. As of the date of this Term Sheet, no options, warrants, convertible securities, or other instruments convertible into or exercisable or exchangeable for equity interests of the Company are outstanding, and Seller shall represent and warrant to such effect in the Definitive Agreement. Following the Closing (as defined below), the Company will be a wholly-owned subsidiary of Buyer.

**Definitive Agreement.** The transaction shall be documented in a definitive Stock Purchase Agreement (the \"Definitive Agreement\" or the \"SPA\"), which shall be prepared in the first instance by Seller\'s counsel, Fortuna & Blake LLP, and delivered to Buyer\'s counsel, Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP, for review and negotiation. The Definitive Agreement shall contain the terms and conditions set forth in this Term Sheet, together with such additional terms and conditions as are customary for transactions of this nature and as may be mutually agreed by the parties. The Definitive Agreement shall be consistent with the terms of this Term Sheet in all material respects. In the event of a conflict between this Term Sheet and the Definitive Agreement, the parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve such conflict; provided, however, that the economic terms set forth herein (including without limitation the Base Enterprise Value, the purchase price formula, the indemnification cap and basket, the Special Indemnity terms, the escrow terms, and the earnout terms) shall control until expressly superseded by a mutually executed Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 3: Purchase Price]{.underline}**
**Base Enterprise Value.** The base enterprise value of the Company for purposes of this transaction shall be Two Hundred Fifteen Million Dollars (\$215,000,000) (the \"Base Enterprise Value\").
**Purchase Price Formula.** The purchase price to be paid by Buyer to Seller for the Shares (the \"Purchase Price\") shall be calculated as follows:
> Purchase Price = Base Enterprise Value + Estimated Closing Net Working Capital -- Estimated Closing Indebtedness -- Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses

**Target Net Working Capital.** The target net working capital for the Company (the \"Target NWC\") shall be Eighteen Million Two Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,200,000), calculated in accordance with the methodology to be set forth in the Definitive Agreement and consistent with United States generally accepted accounting principles (\"GAAP\") as historically applied by the Company.

**Estimated Closing Statement.** Seller shall deliver to Buyer a good faith estimated closing statement (the \"Estimated Closing Statement\") setting forth Seller\'s reasonable estimates of (i) Closing Net Working Capital (\"Estimated Closing NWC\"), (ii) Closing Indebtedness (\"Estimated Closing Indebtedness\"), and (iii) Seller Transaction Expenses (\"Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses\"), in each case calculated as of the Closing Date, no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. The Estimated Closing Statement shall be prepared in accordance with GAAP as historically applied by the Company and in a manner consistent with the methodology to be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**Illustrative Calculation.** The following calculation is provided for reference purposes only and shall not be deemed to establish the actual Purchase Price or any component thereof:
**Component**                                 **Amount**
Base Enterprise Value                         \$215,000,000
Plus: Estimated Closing NWC                   \$18,200,000
Less: Estimated Closing Indebtedness          (\$42,300,000)
Less: Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses   (\$3,900,000)
**Estimated Closing Payment**                 **\$187,000,000**
For reference, the components of Estimated Closing Indebtedness and Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses used in the illustrative calculation above are as follows:
> *Estimated Closing Indebtedness (\$42,300,000):*
> • Senior term loan with Cascade Mutual Bank: \$28,000,000
> • Equipment financing with Pacific Lease Corp.: \$9,800,000
> • Subordinated seller note payable to Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.: \$4,500,000
> *Estimated Seller Transaction Expenses (\$3,900,000):*
> • Seller\'s legal fees (Fortuna & Blake LLP): \$1,800,000
> • Seller\'s advisory fees: \$1,200,000
> • Other transaction costs (including accounting, transfer taxes, and miscellaneous): \$900,000

**Net Working Capital Adjustment.** The net working capital adjustment shall be calculated on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar (i.e., there shall be no collar or threshold). Following the Closing, Buyer shall prepare a final closing statement reflecting the actual Closing NWC, Closing Indebtedness, and Seller Transaction Expenses as of the Closing Date. The post-closing true-up process shall be completed within ninety (90) days following the Closing Date. Standard dispute resolution procedures, including referral to an independent accounting firm mutually acceptable to the parties for resolution of any disputed items, shall be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 4: Escrow]{.underline}**

**Escrow Amount.** At the Closing, Buyer shall deposit Sixteen Million One Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$16,125,000) (the \"Escrow Amount\"), which is equal to seven and one-half percent (7.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value (\$215,000,000 × 0.075 = \$16,125,000), with Pinnacle Trust Company, as escrow agent (the \"Escrow Agent\"), pursuant to an escrow agreement in customary form and substance to be agreed upon by the parties and the Escrow Agent (the \"Escrow Agreement\"). The Escrow Amount shall be deducted from the Purchase Price payable to Seller at Closing.

**Escrow Purpose.** The Escrow Amount shall serve as security for Seller\'s indemnification obligations under the Definitive Agreement. The Escrow Amount shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for Buyer\'s indemnification claims with respect to breaches of non-Fundamental Representations, up to the Escrow Amount; provided that claims for Losses exceeding the Escrow Amount (but subject to the Cap set forth in Section 8 below) may be pursued directly against Seller. For the avoidance of doubt, the escrow shall also serve as a source of recovery for claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity as set forth in Section 9 below.
**Escrow Release Schedule.** The Escrow Amount shall be released in accordance with the following schedule:

> \(a\) *General Indemnification Claims (Non-Fundamental Representations):* The portion of the Escrow Amount allocable to general indemnification claims shall be released to Seller on the date that is eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date, less any amounts subject to pending and unresolved indemnification claims as of such date.

> \(b\) *Fundamental Representations and Special Indemnities:* The portion of the Escrow Amount allocable to Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be released to Seller on the date that is thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, less any amounts subject to pending and unresolved indemnification claims as of such date.

Any portion of the Escrow Amount that is not subject to pending or unresolved indemnification claims as of the applicable release date shall be promptly released to Seller. The specific allocation of the Escrow Amount between general indemnification claims and Fundamental Representations/Special Indemnity claims shall be set forth in the Escrow Agreement.
**[Section 5: Earnout]{.underline}**

**Maximum Earnout Payment.** In addition to the Purchase Price, Buyer shall pay to Seller an earnout payment (the \"Earnout Payment\") of up to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000), subject to the terms and conditions set forth below.

**Measurement Period.** The Earnout Payment shall be calculated based on the Company\'s financial performance during the trailing twelve-month (TTM) period ending December 31, 2026 (the \"Measurement Period\").

**Metric.** The Earnout Payment shall be based on the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period. \"Adjusted EBITDA\" shall be calculated in a manner consistent with the Company\'s historical practice and as defined in the Definitive Agreement, and shall exclude the impact of purchase price accounting adjustments, transaction-related costs, integration costs, and any other items mutually agreed to be excluded by the parties as set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**Threshold and Floor.**

> \(a\) *Full Earnout:* If the Company achieves TTM Adjusted EBITDA of Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000) or more for the Measurement Period, the full Earnout Payment of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) shall be payable to Seller.
> \(b\) *Floor:* No Earnout Payment shall be payable if TTM Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is less than Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000).

> \(c\) *Pro-Rata Calculation:* If TTM Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is equal to or greater than Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), the Earnout Payment shall be calculated on a linear interpolation basis in accordance with the following formula:
> which equals approximately \$4,166,667 per \$1,000,000 of Adjusted EBITDA above \$32,000,000.

**Earnout Covenant.** Buyer shall not take any action with the primary purpose of avoiding or reducing the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, Buyer shall have no affirmative obligation to operate the Company\'s business in any particular manner, and nothing herein shall restrict Buyer\'s ability to operate, integrate, or restructure the Company\'s business in Buyer\'s sole discretion, provided that Buyer does not take actions with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. The Definitive Agreement shall not impose on Buyer any obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, to maintain any particular level of capital expenditure, to retain any particular employees, or to refrain from any particular operational decisions, so long as any such actions are taken in the ordinary course of Buyer\'s management of the Company and not with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment.

**Payment.** The Earnout Payment, if any, shall be payable to Seller within sixty (60) days following the end of the Measurement Period. Buyer shall deliver to Seller a written calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period, together with reasonable supporting detail, within forty-five (45) days following the end of the Measurement Period.
**Dispute Resolution.** Customary earnout dispute resolution procedures, including review by an independent accounting firm, shall be set forth in the Definitive Agreement.
**[Section 6: Closing Indebtedness Payoff Mechanics]{.underline}**

**Payoff Letters Required.** Seller shall deliver to Buyer, or shall cause to be delivered to Buyer, executed payoff letters from each holder of Target Indebtedness (including, without limitation, Cascade Mutual Bank (in respect of the senior term loan), Pacific Lease Corp. (in respect of the equipment financing), and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. (in respect of the subordinated seller note)) no later than three (3) business days prior to the Closing Date. Each payoff letter shall set forth, at a minimum: (i) the aggregate amount required to repay in full the applicable indebtedness as of the Closing Date (including all principal, accrued and unpaid interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, and any other amounts required to fully satisfy and discharge such indebtedness), (ii) wire transfer instructions for payment of the applicable payoff amount, and (iii) a commitment by the applicable lender or holder to release all liens, security interests, mortgages, pledges, and other encumbrances securing such indebtedness upon receipt of the payoff amount, together with such UCC-3 termination statements, lien release documents, and other instruments as may be required to evidence such release.

**Simultaneous Payoff at Closing.** All Target Indebtedness shall be repaid simultaneously at Closing through the closing funds flow. No Target Indebtedness shall remain outstanding following the Closing. Buyer shall cause the payoff amounts to be paid directly to the applicable lenders or holders at Closing in accordance with the wire transfer instructions set forth in the payoff letters.

**Funds Flow Agreement.** The parties shall negotiate and execute a funds flow agreement (the \"Funds Flow Agreement\") at least two (2) business days prior to the Closing Date, setting forth the exact dollar amounts and wire transfer instructions for all payments to be made at the Closing, including, without limitation: (a) repayment of all Target Indebtedness, (b) payment of all Seller Transaction Expenses, (c) deposit of the Escrow Amount with Pinnacle Trust Company, and (d) payment of the balance of the Purchase Price (after giving effect to the foregoing deductions) to Seller.

**Condition to Closing.** Delivery of payoff letters as described above shall be a condition to Buyer\'s obligation to consummate the Closing. In the event Seller fails to deliver any required payoff letter within the timeframe specified above, Buyer shall have the right, in its sole discretion, to (x) waive such condition and proceed with the Closing, or (y) delay the Closing until such payoff letter is delivered, subject to the Outside Date.
**[Section 7: Representations and Warranties]{.underline}**

**Seller\'s Representations and Warranties.** Seller shall make customary representations and warranties in the Definitive Agreement regarding Seller\'s authority to execute and deliver the Definitive Agreement and consummate the transactions contemplated thereby, the enforceability of the Definitive Agreement against Seller, Seller\'s valid title to the Shares (free and clear of all liens and encumbrances), and the absence of conflicts with Seller\'s organizational documents, material contracts, and applicable law (collectively, the \"Fundamental Representations\").

**Company Representations and Warranties.** The Definitive Agreement shall contain representations and warranties relating to the Company, which shall include, without limitation, representations regarding: organization and good standing; capitalization; financial statements (including the audited financial statements of the Company for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2022, 2023, and 2024); absence of undisclosed liabilities; compliance with applicable laws and regulations; environmental matters (including, without limitation, environmental permits, environmental liabilities, compliance with CERCLA and other environmental laws, and the use, storage, treatment, and disposal of hazardous materials); material contracts; intellectual property; employee and labor matters (including benefit plans); tax matters; owned and leased real property; insurance coverage; government contracts and compliance; and the absence of any Material Adverse Effect since December 31, 2024. The specific scope, detail, and materiality qualifiers applicable to each representation and warranty shall be negotiated and set forth in the Definitive Agreement, subject to the indemnification and survival terms set forth in this Term Sheet.

**Buyer\'s Representations and Warranties.** Buyer shall make customary representations and warranties in the Definitive Agreement regarding Buyer\'s authority, enforceability of the Definitive Agreement against Buyer, and the sufficiency of Buyer\'s financing to consummate the transactions contemplated hereby.
**[Section 8: Indemnification]{.underline}**

**Seller\'s Indemnification Obligations.** Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its affiliates (including, following the Closing, the Company and its subsidiaries), and their respective officers, directors, managers, members, employees, agents, and representatives (collectively, the \"Buyer Indemnified Parties\") from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, claims, demands, judgments, settlements, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses) (collectively, \"Losses\") arising from, relating to, or in connection with: (i) any breach of or inaccuracy in any of Seller\'s representations and warranties contained in the Definitive Agreement, (ii) any breach of or failure to perform any of Seller\'s covenants or agreements contained in the Definitive Agreement, and (iii) the Special Indemnities described in Section 9 of this Term Sheet.

**General Indemnification Cap.** Seller\'s aggregate indemnification liability for Losses arising from breaches of non-Fundamental Representations shall not exceed twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value, which equals Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$26,875,000) (\$215,000,000 × 0.125 = \$26,875,000) (the \"General Cap\"). For the avoidance of doubt, the parties have agreed that the general indemnification cap shall be twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

**Fundamental Representations Cap.** Seller\'s aggregate indemnification liability for Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations shall not exceed the Purchase Price (as finally determined following completion of the post-closing true-up process described in Section 3).

**Basket (True Deductible).** Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification for Losses arising from breaches of non-Fundamental Representations until the aggregate amount of such Losses exceeds one percent (1.0%) of the Base Enterprise Value, which equals Two Million One Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,150,000) (\$215,000,000 × 0.01 = \$2,150,000) (the \"Deductible\"). Once the aggregate amount of such Losses exceeds the Deductible, Buyer shall be entitled to indemnification only for Losses in excess of the Deductible (i.e., the basket shall operate as a true deductible, not a tipping basket or first-dollar basket). The Deductible shall not apply to Losses arising from (a) breaches of Fundamental Representations, (b) the Special Indemnities described in Section 9, or (c) claims arising from fraud or willful misconduct.
**Survival Periods.** The representations and warranties contained in the Definitive Agreement shall survive the Closing for the following periods:
> \(a\) *Fundamental Representations:* Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing until the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations plus sixty (60) days.

> \(b\) *Non-Fundamental Representations (General):* Non-Fundamental Representations (other than environmental representations) shall survive the Closing for a period of eighteen (18) months following the Closing Date.

> \(c\) *Environmental Representations:* The survival period for environmental representations and warranties shall be negotiated and set forth in the Definitive Agreement, but shall in no event be less than thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date. Buyer reserves the right to seek survival of environmental representations through the full applicable statute of limitations.
> \(d\) *Covenants:* Covenants shall survive for the applicable performance period plus twelve (12) months, or such longer period as may be specified in the Definitive Agreement.
> \(e\) *Special Indemnities:* The survival period for the Special Indemnities shall be as set forth in Section 9 below.

**Sole Remedy.** Indemnification as set forth in the Definitive Agreement shall be the sole and exclusive post-Closing remedy of the parties for any breach of or inaccuracy in any representation or warranty contained in the Definitive Agreement, other than in the case of actual fraud or willful misconduct. Nothing in this Section 8 or in the Definitive Agreement shall limit any party\'s right to seek equitable relief, including specific performance and injunctive relief, as may be available at law or in equity.
**Escrow as Source of Recovery.** The Escrow Amount shall serve as a source of recovery for indemnification claims as described in Section 4 of this Term Sheet.
**[Section 9: Special Indemnity --- Dalton Creek CERCLA Matter]{.underline}**

**Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.** In addition to, and not subject to the limitations set forth in, the general indemnification provisions described in Section 8 above, Seller shall provide a special indemnity (the \"Dalton Creek Special Indemnity\") with respect to all Losses arising from, related to, or in connection with:

> \(i\) the pending information request from the United States Environmental Protection Agency (\"EPA\") under Section 104(e) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act, as amended (\"CERCLA\"), regarding the Company\'s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon (the \"Dalton Creek Facility\");

> \(ii\) any enforcement action, claim, investigation, order, consent decree, administrative order, or proceeding by any Governmental Authority or any third party relating to or arising out of the Company\'s operations, activities, or waste disposal practices at the Dalton Creek Facility; and

> \(iii\) any environmental contamination, remediation obligations, natural resource damages, response costs, or other liabilities associated with the Company\'s former operations at the Dalton Creek Facility, whether arising under CERCLA, the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act, the Oregon Environmental Cleanup Law, or any other federal, state, or local environmental law.

**Not Subject to Basket or Cap.** The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be subject to the Deductible or the General Cap set forth in Section 8 above. The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, Seller\'s other indemnification obligations under the Definitive Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, Losses indemnifiable under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be counted toward, or reduce, the General Cap or the Deductible.
**Survival.** The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall survive the Closing for a period of seventy-two (72) months (six (6) years) following the Closing Date.

**Escrow Holdback.** A portion of the Escrow Amount shall be available to satisfy claims under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, with such portion held for thirty-six (36) months following the Closing Date, as set forth in Section 4 above. For the avoidance of doubt, Buyer\'s right to recover under the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall not be limited to the Escrow Amount, and Buyer shall be entitled to pursue claims against Seller directly for any Losses in excess of the available escrow funds.

**Background.** For reference, Seller has disclosed to Buyer the pending EPA information request under CERCLA Section 104(e) relating to the Dalton Creek Facility. Outside environmental counsel retained by the Company, Haverford Environmental Law Group, has estimated the Company\'s potential liability in connection with the Dalton Creek matter to be in the range of One Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,500,000) to Six Million Dollars (\$6,000,000). The Company maintains an environmental impairment liability insurance policy with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. (Policy No. EIL-2024-0093712), with an aggregate limit of Fifteen Million Dollars (\$15,000,000) and a per-occurrence limit of Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000). The Definitive Agreement shall include provisions regarding the maintenance and application of such insurance coverage.
**[Section 10: Representations and Warranties Insurance]{.underline}**

**R&W Insurance Policy.** Buyer intends to obtain a representations and warranties insurance policy (the \"R&W Insurance Policy\") from Granite Ridge Underwriters (or such other insurer as Buyer may select in its sole discretion) in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Term Sheet and the Definitive Agreement. The cost of the R&W Insurance Policy (including all premiums, underwriting fees, broker fees, taxes, and other amounts payable in connection with the placement of such policy) shall be borne solely by Buyer. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to bind the R&W Insurance Policy on or prior to the Closing Date.

**Subrogation Waiver.** The Definitive Agreement shall include a provision pursuant to which Buyer agrees, and shall cause the R&W Insurance carrier to agree, that the R&W Insurance carrier shall waive, and shall not exercise, any right of subrogation against Seller or any of Seller\'s affiliates, officers, directors, employees, agents, or representatives with respect to any claim made under the R&W Insurance Policy, except in the case of actual fraud by Seller. This subrogation waiver shall survive the Closing and shall be included as a covenant of Buyer in the Definitive Agreement.

**Cooperation.** Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, reasonably cooperate with Buyer and the R&W Insurance carrier in connection with the underwriting and placement of the R&W Insurance Policy. Such cooperation shall include, without limitation, (a) providing access to the Company\'s management team, including Patricia Huang and Robert Merrill, for underwriting interviews, (b) making available such documents, data, reports, and other information as may be reasonably requested by the R&W Insurance carrier in connection with its underwriting review, and (c) responding in a timely manner to reasonable follow-up inquiries from the R&W Insurance carrier. Seller\'s cooperation obligations under this Section 10 shall not require Seller to incur any unreasonable out-of-pocket expense (other than de minimis costs) without Buyer\'s prior agreement to reimburse such expense.
**[Section 11: Non-Competition; Non-Solicitation]{.underline}**

**Non-Competition.** The Definitive Agreement shall include a covenant pursuant to which Seller and its controlled affiliates shall agree not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, subject to the following parameters:
> \(a\) *Duration:* Three (3) years following the Closing Date.
> \(b\) *Geographic Scope:* The States of Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada.
> \(c\) *Business Scope:* Environmental remediation services and hazardous waste management services, as such services are conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date.

> \(d\) *Bound Parties:* Seller and its controlled affiliates. For the avoidance of doubt, the non-competition covenant shall not apply to any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation or hazardous waste management as of the Closing Date.
**Carve-Outs.** The non-competition covenant shall not restrict Seller or its affiliates from:
> \(i\) conducting their existing construction and timber operations, as such operations are conducted as of the Closing Date;
> \(ii\) holding passive investments of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity; or

> \(iii\) performing environmental-related activities that are incidental to and performed solely in connection with Seller\'s construction or timber operations (e.g., erosion control, stormwater management, and environmental compliance activities performed on Seller\'s own construction or timber sites).
