matches.line: Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP\'s Environmental Practice Group has completed its environmental due diligence review of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. (\"Cascadia\" or the \"Company\"), an Oregon corporation headquartered at 8700 SW Tualatin-Sherwood Road, Suite 200, Tualatin, Oregon 97062. Cascadia provides environmental remediation, hazardous waste management, and environmental consulting services, operating through seven offices located in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. The Company employs approximately 340 full-time employees across these operations.

1\. **Dalton Creek CERCLA Exposure (HIGH RISK).** The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has issued an information request under CERCLA § 104(e) to Cascadia regarding the Company\'s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility. Although no formal enforcement action or PRP designation has been issued to date, the § 104(e) letter is a well-recognized precursor to potential enforcement activity. We estimate Cascadia\'s potential liability exposure in the range of \$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000, depending upon EPA\'s cost allocation approach and the solvency of other potentially responsible parties.

2\. **Hargrove Industrial Site Remediation (MODERATE RISK).** Cascadia is actively performing environmental remediation at the former Hargrove Industrial Site in Milwaukie, Oregon, under contract with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality. Estimated remaining remediation costs total approximately \$4,200,000. This exposure is a contractual obligation and is covered by a site-specific environmental liability insurance policy with a \$10,000,000 policy limit, which appears adequate.

3\. **Environmental Permit Portfolio (MODERATE RISK).** Cascadia holds 23 active environmental permits across four states. Although the transaction is structured as a stock purchase, multiple state environmental regulatory programs require notification to or approval from the issuing agency upon a change in control of the permit holder. Failure to comply with these requirements could result in permit violations, enforcement actions, or permit revocation.

4\. **Government Contract Regulatory Compliance (HIGH RISK).** Cascadia is party to four active government contracts with the Oregon DEQ, Washington Department of Ecology, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management. The two federal contracts are subject to the Anti-Assignment Act and the Federal Acquisition Regulation\'s novation requirements under FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12. Failure to obtain required novations could result in contract termination, eliminating a material revenue stream.

> • **Environmental Site Assessments.** Phase I and Phase II environmental site assessments for all seven of the Company\'s office and operational locations in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada.

> • **Environmental Permits.** Copies of all 23 active environmental remediation permits held by the Company across four states, including RCRA permits, NPDES permits, Clean Air Act emissions permits, state hazardous waste transporter permits, and state remediation contractor licenses.

> • **CERCLA Correspondence.** The EPA\'s CERCLA § 104(e) information request regarding the Dalton Creek disposal facility, dated February 12, 2025, together with the Company\'s written response thereto and all related internal correspondence and records.

> • **Remediation Contracts.** All remediation contracts, statements of work, and work plans pertaining to the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation project, including the master contract with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality and applicable task orders.

> • **Insurance Policies.** Environmental impairment liability insurance policies issued by Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. to the Company, including the general environmental impairment liability policy (aggregate limit of \$15,000,000; per-occurrence limit of \$5,000,000) and the site-specific environmental liability insurance policy covering the Hargrove Industrial Site (policy limit of \$10,000,000).

> • **Government Contracts.** Copies of all four active government contracts between the Company and the Oregon DEQ, Washington Department of Ecology, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and Bureau of Land Management, including all modifications, amendments, and task orders.

> • **Professional Licenses.** Records pertaining to professional engineer (PE) licenses held by 12 employees identified as critical to maintaining permit compliance and performing permitted activities.
**[III. Dalton Creek Disposal Facility --- CERCLA Exposure]{.underline}**

Cascadia formerly operated at the Dalton Creek disposal facility, a former hazardous waste disposal site located in Clackamas County, Oregon. The Company\'s operations at Dalton Creek involved the handling, treatment, and disposal of hazardous wastes generated by third-party industrial customers. These operations significantly predate the current management team and were conducted during a period when the Company was under different operational leadership. According to records produced during due diligence and confirmed by management interviews, Cascadia ceased all operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility in approximately 2015.

In February 2025, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Region 10, issued an information request to Cascadia under Section 104(e) of the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980, as amended (\"CERCLA\"), 42 U.S.C. § 9604(e). The information request seeks comprehensive documentation of the Company\'s waste handling and disposal activities at the Dalton Creek facility, including waste manifests, disposal records, volume and characterization data, and operational history during the period of the Company\'s use of the site.

As of the date of this memorandum, no formal enforcement action, notice of potential responsible party (\"PRP\") designation, unilateral administrative order, or lawsuit has been filed or issued by EPA or any other party against Cascadia in connection with the Dalton Creek facility. However, the issuance of a § 104(e) information request is widely recognized as a standard precursor to potential PRP designation and subsequent enforcement activity under CERCLA. The Company\'s management confirmed that it has retained outside environmental counsel to assist with the response to the information request and to monitor developments at the site.

Based on our review of the Company\'s records, the EPA information request and the Company\'s response, publicly available site information, and consultation with environmental counsel experienced in CERCLA cost allocation proceedings, we estimate Cascadia\'s potential liability exposure in connection with the Dalton Creek disposal facility to be in the range of **\$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000**. The factors underlying this range are as follows:

> • **Low End (\$1,500,000).** This estimate assumes that EPA pursues a multi-party cost allocation among all identified potentially responsible parties at the Dalton Creek site, that Cascadia\'s proportionate share of total cleanup costs is determined on the basis of the volume and toxicity of waste it disposed at the facility, and that other identified PRPs remain solvent and capable of bearing their respective shares. Under this scenario, Cascadia\'s share would represent a minority allocation consistent with its relative contribution to site contamination.

> • **High End (\$6,000,000).** This estimate reflects the possibility that EPA may designate Cascadia as a major contributor to the contamination at the site, or that one or more other PRPs may prove financially unable to satisfy their allocated shares. Under CERCLA § 107, liability is joint and several, meaning that EPA may seek recovery of the full cost of remediation from any single PRP, regardless of that party\'s proportionate contribution. If other PRPs are insolvent or unidentifiable, Cascadia\'s exposure could increase significantly. The high-end estimate also accounts for the possibility that the overall scope and cost of site remediation may exceed current projections.

It is important to note that CERCLA proceedings frequently extend over many years. Under CERCLA § 113(g)(2), the statute of limitations for a cost recovery action is six years from the date of completion of a remedial action at the site. Contribution claims under § 113(f) may extend further depending on the timing of settlement or judgment. Given that no formal remedial action has been initiated at the Dalton Creek site, it is possible that Cascadia\'s ultimate liability will not be determined for a period of years following the closing of the proposed transaction.

The Company\'s environmental impairment liability insurance with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. (aggregate limit \$15,000,000; per-occurrence limit \$5,000,000) may provide coverage for defense costs and some portion of the Company\'s ultimate liability in connection with the Dalton Creek matter. However, coverage for legacy disposal operations is commonly subject to policy exclusions, including prior-knowledge exclusions, pollution date restrictions, and exclusions for known or disclosed conditions. We recommend that insurance counsel conduct a detailed review of the applicable policy terms to determine the extent and reliability of available coverage.
**[C. SPA Recommendations --- Dalton Creek]{.underline}**
Based on the foregoing analysis, we make the following recommendations with respect to the treatment of the Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure in the Stock Purchase Agreement:

**Recommendation 1 --- Special Indemnity.** Given the magnitude of the potential exposure (\$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000), the fact that this is a known and disclosed environmental liability arising from Seller\'s period of ownership, and the inherent uncertainty and protracted timeline of CERCLA proceedings, we **strongly recommend** that the SPA include a **Special Indemnity** obligating Seller to indemnify Buyer for all Losses arising from or related to the Dalton Creek disposal facility and the EPA\'s CERCLA § 104(e) information request, including without limitation all costs of investigation, remediation, defense, settlement, contribution, and related administrative proceedings. The Special Indemnity should be structured as follows:

> \(a\) **Survival Period.** The Special Indemnity should survive for no less than **72 months** following the closing date, in order to account for the characteristically lengthy timeline of CERCLA proceedings and the six-year statute of limitations for CERCLA cost recovery actions under § 113(g)(2). A shorter survival period would create an unacceptable risk that Buyer\'s indemnification rights expire before a formal CERCLA claim crystallizes.

> \(b\) **Exclusion from General Basket and Cap.** The Special Indemnity should **not** be subject to the general indemnification deductible basket or aggregate liability cap. The Dalton Creek matter is a known, quantifiable exposure that should be indemnified on a dollar-for-dollar basis from the first dollar of Loss. Subjecting this exposure to general basket and cap limitations would improperly shift a portion of the known risk to Buyer.

> \(d\) **Consistency with Term Sheet.** We note that the executed term sheet dated September 10, 2025, between Whitmore Capital Partners LLC and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc., specifically provides for a \"Special Indemnity\" to address the Dalton Creek matter. The SPA must implement this agreed-upon commercial term. Omission of the Special Indemnity from the Seller\'s initial SPA draft would represent a departure from the agreed deal terms.

**Recommendation 2 --- Extended Survival of Environmental Representations.** Independent of and in addition to the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, the environmental representations and warranties in the SPA should survive for a minimum of **36 months** post-closing, and ideally for the **full applicable statute of limitations** for environmental claims. We understand that seller-favorable first drafts in the middle market typically propose a 12-month survival period for representations and warranties, including environmental representations. For a company whose core business is the provision of environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services, a 12-month survival period for environmental representations would be wholly inadequate for the following reasons:
> \(a\) The Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure may not crystallize into a formal claim, enforcement action, or PRP designation for a period of years following closing, as discussed in Section III.B above.

> \(b\) Cascadia\'s active remediation projects, including the Hargrove Industrial Site project, have multi-year performance timelines during which new environmental liabilities or breaches of environmental representations may emerge.

> \(c\) Environmental liabilities in the remediation services sector routinely emerge well beyond a 12-month period due to the nature of contamination migration, delayed regulatory action, and evolving site characterization data.

> \(d\) For a company whose entire value proposition is built upon environmental compliance and permitting, the environmental representations are among the most critical representations in the agreement and should be afforded extended protection commensurate with that importance.
**[IV. Hargrove Industrial Site Remediation]{.underline}**

Cascadia is currently performing active environmental remediation at the former Hargrove Industrial Site, located in Milwaukie, Oregon, under a remediation services contract with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (\"Oregon DEQ\"). The Hargrove project involves soil and groundwater remediation activities at the former industrial site, including excavation and off-site disposal of contaminated soil, installation and operation of a groundwater extraction and treatment system, and ongoing environmental monitoring. The Company estimates the total remaining cost to complete the remediation at approximately **\$4,200,000**, with the project expected to continue for approximately 18 to 24 months beyond the anticipated closing date. The Hargrove remediation contract is one of the Company\'s four active government contracts and represents a significant ongoing commitment of Company resources and personnel.

Cascadia carries a site-specific environmental liability insurance policy issued by **Northshore Specialty Insurance Co.** with a **\$10,000,000 policy limit** specifically covering the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation project. This policy provides coverage for remediation costs, cost overruns, and third-party claims arising from the Company\'s remediation activities at the Hargrove site. Separately, the Company\'s broader environmental impairment liability insurance with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. carries an aggregate limit of \$15,000,000 and a per-occurrence limit of \$5,000,000. The site-specific Hargrove policy appears adequate to cover the estimated remaining \$4,200,000 remediation cost plus potential cost overruns and third-party claims, assuming no policy exclusions or coverage defenses are applicable. We recommend that the SPA include a representation that all environmental insurance policies maintained by the Company are in full force and effect, that all premiums due have been paid, and that no notice of cancellation, non-renewal, or material modification has been received. The SPA should also include a pre-closing covenant requiring the Company to maintain all such policies through and following the closing date.

We assess the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation project as a **moderate risk** item. The project is a standard remediation engagement being performed under a government contract with the Oregon DEQ. The principal risks are (i) cost overruns in excess of the current \$4,200,000 estimate, (ii) potential regulatory enforcement action if the Company fails to meet remediation milestones established in the work plan and consent order, and (iii) third-party claims arising from remediation activities. The available insurance coverage appears adequate to mitigate these risks. We note that the Oregon DEQ contract under which the Hargrove work is being performed is one of the four government contracts requiring novation or consent analysis, as discussed in Section VI below.
Cascadia holds **23 active environmental remediation permits** across four states: Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. The permit portfolio includes the following categories:

> • **RCRA Permits.** Treatment, storage, and disposal (TSD) facility permits issued under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act and corresponding state programs, authorizing the Company to handle, treat, store, and dispose of hazardous wastes at specified locations.

> • **Clean Water Act Discharge Permits.** National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits authorizing the Company to discharge treated water and stormwater from remediation project sites in compliance with applicable effluent limitations.
> • **Clean Air Act Emissions Permits.** Permits authorizing air emissions from remediation equipment, thermal treatment units, and related operations at Company facilities and project sites.

> • **State Remediation Contractor Licenses and Permits.** State-specific licenses and permits required to perform environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services as a licensed contractor.

All 23 permits are held in the name of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. In addition, 12 of the Company\'s employees hold professional engineer (\"PE\") licenses that are critical to maintaining permit compliance and performing permitted activities. Several of the Company\'s permits are conditioned upon the availability of a PE-licensed professional to oversee permitted operations. Loss of these PE-licensed employees, whether through attrition, termination, or failure to transfer to the post-closing entity, could jeopardize the Company\'s standing under certain permits and impair its ability to perform permitted work.

Although this transaction is structured as a **stock purchase** --- and therefore the legal entity holding the permits (Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.) will not change --- many state environmental regulatory programs nonetheless require **notification to or approval from the issuing agency** upon a change in the ownership or control of the permit holder. This is a critical issue that must be addressed in the SPA. The applicable state-specific requirements include:

> • **Oregon.** Oregon DEQ regulations require notification of a change of ownership or control of a permitted facility within 30 days of such change. Certain RCRA permits issued by Oregon DEQ may require formal transfer approval prior to the change taking effect. *See* OAR Chapter 340, Division 012 and applicable permit conditions.

> • **Washington.** The Washington Department of Ecology requires prior written notification for changes in control of permitted entities. Certain permits include conditions that expressly require agency approval of ownership changes before the transfer is deemed valid. *See* WAC Chapter 173-303 and applicable permit conditions.

> • **California.** The California Department of Toxic Substances Control (\"DTSC\") and regional water quality control boards often require notification and, in certain permit categories, prior approval for changes in control of entities holding hazardous waste facility permits and waste discharge requirements. The specific requirements vary by permit type and issuing authority.

> • **Nevada.** The Nevada Division of Environmental Protection requires notification of ownership changes for certain categories of environmental permits, including hazardous waste management permits and water pollution control permits.

Even in a stock acquisition, these agencies may treat a change of the ultimate parent company --- here, the acquisition of Cascadia\'s shares by Whitmore Capital Partners LLC from Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. --- as a \"change of ownership or control\" that triggers notification or approval requirements under the applicable permit or regulation. Failure to comply with these requirements could result in permit violations, enforcement actions, fines, or in extreme cases, permit revocation or suspension. Given that Cascadia\'s business is entirely dependent upon its ability to perform work under these permits, any disruption to the permit portfolio would be material.

We anticipate that the Seller\'s SPA draft, once circulated, will include representations that all necessary environmental permits are held by the Company and are in good standing. However, a mere representation regarding the current status of permits is insufficient to protect Buyer from the risks associated with the change-of-control process. We **strongly recommend** that the SPA include the following provisions:

> \(a\) **Pre-Closing Covenant.** A covenant requiring Seller and the Company, prior to closing, to (i) identify all environmental permits that require change-of-control notification to or approval from the issuing agency, (ii) prepare and submit all required notifications and applications for approval to the appropriate state environmental agencies, and (iii) cooperate with Buyer in providing all information reasonably requested by any such agency in connection with the change-of-control process.

> \(b\) **Post-Closing Cooperation Covenant.** A covenant obligating Seller to cooperate with Buyer following closing in completing any permit transfer, re-issuance, amendment, or notification process required by any governmental authority as a result of the change of control, including executing documents, providing historical information, and participating in agency proceedings as reasonably requested by Buyer.

> \(c\) **Survival.** These covenants should survive closing for at least **12 months**, or such longer period as may be necessary to complete all pending permit transfers and notifications, including any pending agency review or approval processes.

Affirmative covenants addressing the permit transfer and notification process are essential to protect Buyer\'s investment in a business whose value depends on the continuity of its environmental permits.
Cascadia is party to **four active government contracts**, each of which is material to the Company\'s operations and revenue:
> 1\. **Oregon Department of Environmental Quality** --- Environmental remediation services, including the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation project discussed in Section IV above.
> 2\. **Washington Department of Ecology** --- Environmental consulting and remediation services at multiple sites within the State of Washington.
> 3\. **U.S. Army Corps of Engineers** --- Environmental assessment and remediation services at federally owned or managed properties.
> 4\. **Bureau of Land Management** --- Environmental site characterization and remediation services on federal lands managed by BLM.

These four government contracts collectively represent a material portion of Cascadia\'s annual revenue and serve as a foundation for the Company\'s ongoing business operations. Loss of any one or more of these contracts would have a material adverse effect on the Company\'s financial condition and business prospects.

Federal government contracts are subject to the **Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305**, which generally prohibits the transfer or assignment of government contracts without the consent of the contracting officer. While the Anti-Assignment Act has historically been interpreted to apply primarily to assignments of the contract itself (as opposed to changes in corporate ownership), the **Federal Acquisition Regulation (\"FAR\"), Part 42, Subpart 42.12**, specifically addresses changes in the contractor\'s organizational structure, including changes in ownership.

Under **FAR 42.1204**, when a contractor undergoes a change in ownership --- including when a third party acquires the stock of the contractor --- the contractor is required to submit a request for a **novation agreement** (or, in some cases, a **change-of-name agreement**) to the responsible contracting officer. A novation agreement formally recognizes the successor entity and transfers the government\'s contractual rights and obligations to the recognized successor. The key requirements under FAR 42.12 include:

> • **FAR 42.1204(a).** The contractor must submit a written request for novation to the responsible contracting officer, accompanied by supporting documentation including the acquisition agreement (or relevant portions thereof), a list of all affected contracts, and evidence of the transferee\'s technical and financial capability to perform.
> • **FAR 42.1204(e).** The contracting officer must make an affirmative determination that recognizing the successor is in the government\'s interest before executing the novation agreement.

> • **Interim Period.** Until a novation agreement is executed, the government may continue to treat the original contractor as the responsible party under the contract. Failure to obtain novation could result in the government treating the change of ownership as a breach of the contract, potentially leading to termination for default or termination for convenience.

**For the two federal contracts** --- the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers contract and the Bureau of Land Management contract --- **novation agreements will be required** under FAR 42.12 because Whitmore Capital Partners LLC, a new parent entity with no prior relationship to Cascadia, is acquiring 100% of the outstanding stock of the Company from Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.

**For the two state contracts** --- the Oregon DEQ contract and the Washington Department of Ecology contract --- analogous state procurement regulations may impose similar notification or approval requirements for changes in corporate ownership of a government contractor. The specific requirements depend on the terms of each contract and the applicable state procurement code. These state contracts require further review of their specific provisions and the relevant Oregon and Washington procurement regulations.

**Risk Assessment.** We assess this as a **HIGH RISK** item. Failure to obtain required novation agreements or government consents could result in **contract termination**, which would eliminate a material revenue stream, potentially trigger cross-default provisions under the Company\'s other contracts or financing arrangements, and materially impair the value of Buyer\'s investment. The novation process is not merely administrative --- contracting officers have discretion to deny novation if they determine that the successor entity does not have the capability or resources to perform, or if recognition is not in the government\'s interest.

**Recommendation 1 --- Pre-Closing Covenant.** The SPA should include a specific covenant requiring Seller and the Company to (a) promptly notify each government contracting officer (federal and state) of the contemplated transaction, (b) submit all required novation request packages under FAR 42.12 for the two federal contracts and all analogous submissions required under state procurement regulations for the two state contracts, and (c) use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all required novation agreements, recognition agreements, or government consents prior to closing.

**Recommendation 2 --- Closing Condition or Specific Covenant.** The deal team should carefully consider whether to make completion of the government contract novation process a **condition to closing** or a **pre-closing best-efforts covenant with a post-closing cooperation tail**. Given that the FAR novation process can take 60 to 120 days or longer, requiring full novation completion as a hard closing condition could delay closing beyond the expected mid-January 2026 timeline or the February 28, 2026 outside date set forth in the term sheet. We recommend the following balanced approach:
> \(a\) Require that all novation requests and government notifications have been **submitted** to all relevant contracting officers prior to closing.

> \(b\) Require that no government contracting officer has **denied** a novation request or indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, or materially modify any government contract as a result of the contemplated transaction.

> \(c\) Include a **post-closing cooperation covenant** requiring Seller to continue cooperating in the novation process following closing, including executing documents, providing information, and participating in meetings with contracting officers as reasonably requested by Buyer.

**Recommendation 3 --- Representations.** The SPA should include specific representations that (a) Seller has provided complete and accurate copies of all government contracts, including all modifications, amendments, and task orders, (b) the Company is in material compliance with all terms of such government contracts, (c) no government contract is the subject of any pending or threatened termination, suspension, or debarment proceeding, and (d) to Seller\'s Knowledge, no contracting officer has indicated any intent to terminate, not renew, or materially modify any such contract.

**Recommendation 4 --- Risk Allocation.** If any government contract is terminated as a result of the change of ownership and the failure to obtain the required novation agreement or government consent, the resulting Losses --- including lost revenue, contract penalties, and consequential damages --- should be allocated to Seller through the indemnification provisions of the SPA.

We note that the Seller\'s SPA draft should be carefully reviewed to determine whether the conditions-to-closing article addresses government contract consents separately from general third-party consents. It is common in seller-favorable first drafts to group government contract consents with general commercial consents --- this approach is insufficient given the unique federal regulatory framework applicable to government contracts and the heightened risk of contract termination. Government contract novation should be treated as a distinct and specifically addressed closing requirement.
Cascadia maintains the following environmental insurance program, both policies issued by Northshore Specialty Insurance Co.:

**Environmental Impairment Liability (\"EIL\") Insurance.** The Company\'s general EIL policy provides coverage for third-party claims arising from pollution conditions associated with the Company\'s operations. The policy carries an aggregate limit of \$15,000,000 and a per-occurrence limit of \$5,000,000. The policy covers defense costs, remediation costs, and bodily injury and property damage claims resulting from pollution events. The EIL policy is the Company\'s primary environmental insurance coverage and applies across all of the Company\'s operations and locations.

**Hargrove Site-Specific Policy.** In addition to the general EIL policy, the Company maintains a project-specific environmental liability policy covering the Hargrove Industrial Site remediation project. This policy carries a \$10,000,000 policy limit and provides coverage for remediation costs, cost overruns, and third-party claims arising specifically from the Company\'s remediation activities at the Hargrove site.

As discussed in Section III.B above, coverage for the Dalton Creek matter under the general EIL policy is uncertain. Legacy disposal operations conducted at the Dalton Creek facility may be subject to policy exclusions, including prior-knowledge exclusions, pollution date restrictions, and exclusions for known or previously disclosed environmental conditions. We recommend that insurance counsel be engaged to conduct a detailed review of the EIL policy terms and conditions to determine the extent of available coverage for the Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure and to assess the risk of coverage denial.

We recommend that the SPA include (a) a representation that all environmental insurance policies maintained by the Company are in full force and effect, that all premiums due thereunder have been paid in full, and that no notice of cancellation, non-renewal, or material modification has been received, and (b) a pre-closing covenant requiring the Company to maintain all such policies in full force and effect through and following closing.

1              **Dalton Creek Special Indemnity**                         Indemnification Article                         Add Special Indemnity for all Dalton Creek CERCLA Losses; 72-month survival; not subject to general basket or cap; 36-month escrow holdback with Pinnacle Trust Company. Consistent with term sheet dated September 10, 2025.                                                                                                                       Section III.C

3              **Government Contract Novation**                           Conditions to Closing / Pre-Closing Covenants   Add specific provisions addressing FAR 42.12 novation requirements for the 4 government contracts (Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, US Army Corps of Engineers, Bureau of Land Management). Require submission of novation requests pre-closing; post-closing cooperation covenant; specific representations regarding government contract status.   Section VI.C

4              **Environmental Permit Transfer/Notification Covenants**   Pre-Closing and Post-Closing Covenants          Add pre-closing and post-closing cooperation covenants requiring identification of all permits requiring change-of-control notification, submission of all required notifications, and Seller cooperation in completing permit transfer processes across OR, WA, CA, and NV.                                                                        Section V.B

> • **Insurance Maintenance Covenant.** SPA should include a pre-closing covenant requiring the Company to maintain all environmental insurance policies (EIL and Hargrove site-specific) in full force and effect through closing, with a representation that all premiums have been paid and no notice of cancellation has been received.

> • **Insurance Counsel Review of Dalton Creek Coverage.** Insurance counsel should be engaged promptly to review the EIL policy terms and assess the availability and reliability of coverage for the Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure. The results of this review may affect the sizing of the Special Indemnity escrow.

> • **Environmental Permit Representations.** Confirm that the Seller\'s environmental representations in the SPA specifically cover all 23 active environmental permits, including a representation that each permit is valid, in good standing, and not subject to any pending or threatened revocation, suspension, or modification.

> • **Government Contract Novation as Closing Condition.** Whether completion of the government contract novation process should be a hard closing condition versus a best-efforts pre-closing covenant with a post-closing tail. Making full novation completion a closing condition may delay closing beyond the expected mid-January 2026 timeline or the February 28, 2026 outside date. However, proceeding to close without novation creates a risk of post-closing contract termination. We recommend that Elena Vasquez-Moreno and Marcus Devereaux of Whitmore Capital discuss the appropriate risk allocation.

> • **Dalton Creek Escrow Structure.** Whether the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity escrow should be carved out of the general \$16,125,000 escrow fund or maintained as a separate, dedicated escrow fund with Pinnacle Trust Company. A separate escrow would provide clearer protection for Buyer but may be resisted by Seller as adding administrative complexity.

The environmental due diligence conducted by the Environmental Practice Group has identified material environmental risks associated with the acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. that must be addressed through specific provisions in the Stock Purchase Agreement. The **Dalton Creek CERCLA exposure** and the **government contract novation requirements** are the two highest-priority items and require immediate attention in the deal team\'s SPA markup. The **environmental permit transfer and notification requirements** and the **extended survival of environmental representations** are also essential provisions that must be included to protect Buyer\'s investment.

**Section 2.05 Earnout**

**(a)** *Maximum Earnout Payment.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (the twelve (12) month period ending December 31, 2026) equals or exceeds Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount equal to Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) (the \"Maximum Earnout Payment\").

**(b)** *Pro-Rata Earnout.* If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is at least Thirty-Two Million Dollars (\$32,000,000) but less than Thirty-Eight Million Dollars (\$38,000,000), Buyer shall pay to Seller an amount (the \"Earnout Payment\") equal to: (\$25,000,000 ÷ (\$38,000,000 -- \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA -- \$32,000,000). For the avoidance of doubt, this formula results in a linear interpolation, such that the Earnout Payment increases by approximately Four Million One Hundred Sixty-Six Thousand Six Hundred Sixty-Seven Dollars (\$4,166,667) for each One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) of Adjusted EBITDA in excess of \$32,000,000. If the Company\'s Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period is less than \$32,000,000, no Earnout Payment shall be due or payable.

**(c)** *Earnout Calculation and Dispute Resolution.* Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the \"Earnout Statement\") setting forth Buyer\'s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period, together with reasonable supporting documentation. Seller shall have thirty (30) days to review the Earnout Statement and deliver any objections thereto. The dispute resolution procedures set forth in Section 2.04(b) and Section 2.04(c) shall apply *mutatis mutandis* to any dispute with respect to the Earnout Statement.

**(d)** *Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.* From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Buyer acknowledges and agrees that Seller shall have no obligation to contribute resources, personnel, or funds to the Company during the Earnout Period, and the obligations set forth in this Section 2.05(d) are solely obligations of Buyer.

**(e)** *Payment of Earnout.* Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable pursuant to this Section 2.05 shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period (whether by agreement of the Parties, expiration of the review period without objection, or determination of the Independent Accountant), by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated by Seller. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.

**Section 6.01 Conduct of Business Prior to Closing**

**(a)** From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), except as (i) required by applicable Law, (ii) set forth on Schedule 6.01, or (iii) consented to in writing by Buyer (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), Seller shall cause the Company to:
> \(i\) conduct its business in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice in all material respects;

> \(ii\) use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve intact its business organization, relationships with customers, suppliers, licensors, licensees, Governmental Authorities, and other Persons with whom the Company has material business relationships, and to retain its current officers, key employees, and other key personnel;
> \(iii\) maintain in full force and effect all insurance policies of the Company or replacement policies with comparable coverage on terms no less favorable in the aggregate; and
> \(iv\) maintain its books and records in accordance with past practice and in compliance with applicable Laws.

**(b)** Without limiting the generality of Section 6.01(a), from the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), except as (i) required by applicable Law, (ii) set forth on Schedule 6.01, or (iii) consented to in writing by Buyer (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed), Seller shall not permit the Company to:
> \(i\) amend, modify, or restate the articles of incorporation, bylaws, or other organizational documents of the Company;

> \(ii\) issue, sell, transfer, pledge, dispose of, grant, or authorize the issuance, sale, transfer, pledge, disposition, or grant of any shares of capital stock, or any options, warrants, convertible securities, or other rights to acquire any shares of capital stock, of the Company;

> \(iii\) declare, set aside, authorize, make, or pay any dividend or other distribution (whether in cash, stock, property, or otherwise) in respect of any shares of capital stock of the Company, or repurchase, redeem, or otherwise acquire any shares of capital stock of the Company;
> \(iv\) incur, assume, guarantee, or become liable for any Indebtedness in an amount in excess of \$250,000 individually or \$750,000 in the aggregate;

> \(v\) make any capital expenditures in excess of \$500,000 individually or \$1,500,000 in the aggregate, other than capital expenditures contemplated by the Company\'s approved capital expenditure budget previously provided to Buyer;

> \(vi\) enter into, materially amend, modify, terminate, waive any material rights under, or renew any Company Material Contract (other than renewals in the ordinary course of business on substantially similar terms);

> \(vii\) (A) hire or engage any employee or independent contractor with annual compensation in excess of \$150,000, (B) terminate (other than for cause) any employee with annual compensation in excess of \$150,000, or (C) increase the compensation or benefits of any employee or independent contractor (other than annual merit-based increases in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice for employees earning less than \$150,000 per year);

> \(viii\) settle, compromise, or consent to the entry of judgment in any Action involving payments by or to the Company in excess of \$200,000 or that would impose any non-monetary obligation on the Company;
> \(ix\) change any method of accounting or accounting practice, principle, or policy, except as required by changes in GAAP or applicable Law;

> \(x\) make, change, or revoke any material Tax election, settle or compromise any material Tax claim, audit, or assessment, file any amended Tax Return, or enter into any agreement with a Governmental Authority with respect to Taxes;

> \(xi\) sell, lease, transfer, license, abandon, permit to lapse, or otherwise dispose of any material assets or properties of the Company (other than sales of inventory or obsolete equipment in the ordinary course of business);
> \(xii\) grant, create, incur, assume, or suffer to exist any Encumbrance on any material asset or property of the Company (other than Permitted Encumbrances); or
> \(xiii\) enter into any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusive dealing, or similar restrictive covenant agreement.
**Section 6.02 Access to Information**

From the date of this Agreement until the Closing Date (or the earlier termination of this Agreement in accordance with Article VIII), Seller shall, and shall cause the Company and its officers, directors, employees, accountants, counsel, and other Representatives to, upon reasonable prior notice, afford Buyer and its Representatives reasonable access during normal business hours to the Company\'s properties, offices, plants, other facilities, books, records, contracts, documents, and personnel, and shall furnish to Buyer and its Representatives such additional financial, operating, and other information regarding the Company as Buyer may reasonably request; *provided* that (a) such access shall not unreasonably interfere with the normal operations of the Company, (b) such access shall be conducted in a manner that preserves the confidentiality of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (c) Seller shall not be required to grant access to, or furnish, any information the disclosure of which would (i) violate any applicable Law, (ii) jeopardize any attorney-client privilege or other legal privilege, or (iii) contravene any binding obligation of confidentiality, and (d) all information provided pursuant to this Section 6.02 shall be subject to the terms and conditions of the Confidentiality Agreement.
**Section 6.03 Confidentiality**

The Mutual Confidentiality Agreement, dated as of June 20, 2025, between Seller and Buyer (the \"Confidentiality Agreement\") shall continue in full force and effect in accordance with its terms, and the terms of the Confidentiality Agreement are hereby incorporated herein by reference. If this Agreement is terminated prior to the Closing, the Confidentiality Agreement shall survive such termination in accordance with its terms.
**Section 6.04 HSR Act Filings**

**(a)** Each of Buyer and Seller shall, as promptly as practicable (and in no event later than ten (10) Business Days after the date of this Agreement), file or cause to be filed with the United States Federal Trade Commission and the United States Department of Justice all notifications and other documents and information required to be filed under the HSR Act with respect to the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

**(b)** Buyer and Seller shall each use their reasonable best efforts to (i) obtain early termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act, (ii) comply at the earliest practicable date with any request for additional information and documentary material that may be issued under the HSR Act, (iii) cooperate with the other Party in connection with any filing under the HSR Act and in connection with resolving any investigation or other inquiry of any Governmental Authority under the HSR Act, and (iv) take all actions necessary, proper, or advisable to cause the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act as promptly as practicable.
**(c)** Buyer shall pay all filing fees payable under the HSR Act in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

**(d)** Each Party shall promptly notify the other Party of any substantive communication with, and any inquiry from, any Governmental Authority in connection with the HSR Act filings, and shall provide the other Party with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment on any substantive written communications to any such Governmental Authority prior to submission.
**Section 6.05 Third-Party Consents**

Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain, as promptly as practicable following the date of this Agreement, all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required to be obtained or made in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby, including those set forth on Schedule 4.05. Buyer shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Seller and the Company in connection with obtaining such consents. Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither Seller nor the Company shall be required to pay or commit to pay any amount to (or incur any obligation in favor of) any Person from whom any such consent or waiver may be required (other than filing, application, or similar fees imposed by any Governmental Authority).
**Section 6.06 Public Announcements**

Neither Party shall, and each Party shall cause its respective Affiliates not to, issue any press release or make any public announcement relating to the subject matter of this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed); *provided* that either Party may make any public disclosure that it believes in good faith is required by applicable Law, any listing or trading agreement concerning its publicly traded securities, or any rule or regulation of any securities exchange or self-regulatory organization, in which case the disclosing Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to advise the other Party prior to making the disclosure and to provide the other Party with a reasonable opportunity to review and comment upon such disclosure.
**Section 6.07 Tax Matters**

**(a)** *Pre-Closing Tax Returns.* Seller shall prepare and timely file (or cause to be prepared and timely filed) all Tax Returns of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period that are due (taking into account any valid extensions) after the Closing Date. All such Tax Returns shall be prepared in a manner consistent with past practice (unless otherwise required by applicable Law). Seller shall provide drafts of such Tax Returns to Buyer for its review and comment at least thirty (30) days prior to the due date for filing (or, if such Tax Return is due less than forty-five (45) days after the Closing Date, as soon as reasonably practicable). Seller shall consider in good faith any reasonable comments provided by Buyer. Seller shall timely pay or cause to be paid all Taxes shown as due and payable on such Tax Returns.

**(b)** *Straddle Period Tax Returns.* For any taxable period that includes, but does not end on, the Closing Date (each, a \"Straddle Period\"), the Taxes of the Company attributable to the portion of such Straddle Period ending on and including the Closing Date (the \"Pre-Closing Straddle Amount\") shall be determined using a \"closing-of-the-books\" methodology as of the end of the Closing Date, except that Taxes imposed on a periodic basis (such as real property Taxes) shall be allocated to the Pre-Closing Straddle Amount based on the number of days in the Straddle Period falling on or before the Closing Date relative to the total number of days in such Straddle Period.

625: **Section 7.01 Conditions to Each Party\'s Obligations**
626: 
627: The respective obligations of each Party to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by applicable Law, waiver by each Party) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:
628: 
629: **(a)** No Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action (whether temporary, preliminary, or permanent) that is then in effect and that has the effect of making the transactions contemplated by this Agreement illegal or otherwise preventing or prohibiting the consummation of such transactions.
630: 
631: **(b)** The applicable waiting period (and any extension thereof) under the HSR Act in respect of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall have expired or been terminated.
632: 
633: **(c)** No Action by any Governmental Authority shall be pending that seeks to (i) restrain, enjoin, prevent, prohibit, or make illegal the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (ii) impose limitations on the ability of Buyer to effectively exercise full rights of ownership of the Shares, or (iii) compel Buyer or any of its Affiliates to dispose of or hold separate all or a material portion of the business or assets of the Company.
634: 
635: **Section 7.02 Conditions to Buyer\'s Obligations**
636: 
637: The obligations of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Buyer) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:
638: 
639: **(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* (i) The Fundamental Representations of Seller shall be true and correct in all respects (other than de minimis inaccuracies) as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date, in which case such representation or warranty shall be true and correct as of such earlier date); and (ii) each other representation and warranty of Seller and the Company contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" or \"Material Adverse Effect\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except, in the case of this clause (ii), where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.
640: 
641: **(b)** *Covenants.* Seller shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Seller under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.
642: 
643: **(c)** *No Material Adverse Effect.* Since the date of this Agreement, no event, change, effect, development, condition, or occurrence shall have occurred that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.
644: 
645: **(d)** *Officer\'s Certificate.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer a certificate, signed by a duly authorized officer of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Sections 7.02(a), 7.02(b), and 7.02(c) have been satisfied.
646: 
647: **(e)** *Seller Deliverables.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer all of the closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(a).
648: 
649: **(f)** *Third-Party Consents.* All consents, waivers, approvals, and authorizations set forth on Schedule 4.05 shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect.
650: 
651: **(g)** *Escrow Agreement.* The Escrow Agreement shall have been duly executed and delivered by Seller and the Escrow Agent.
652: 
653: **Section 7.03 Conditions to Seller\'s Obligations**
654: 
655: The obligations of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Seller) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:
656: 
657: **(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* Each representation and warranty of Buyer contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to prevent or materially delay the ability of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.
658: 
659: **(b)** *Covenants.* Buyer shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Buyer under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.
660: 
661: **(c)** *Closing Payments.* Buyer shall have delivered the Closing Payment to Seller and the Escrow Amount to the Escrow Agent in accordance with Section 2.03.
662: 
663: **(d)** *Officer\'s Certificate.* Buyer shall have delivered to Seller a certificate, signed by a duly authorized officer or manager of Buyer, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Sections 7.03(a) and 7.03(b) have been satisfied.
664: 
665: **(e)** *Buyer Deliverables.* Buyer shall have delivered to Seller all of the closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(b).

669: **[TERMINATION]{.underline}**

671: **Section 8.01 Termination**
672: 
673: This Agreement may be terminated at any time prior to the Closing:
674: 
675: **(a)** by the mutual written consent of Buyer and Seller;
676: 
677: **(b)** by either Buyer or Seller, by written notice to the other Party, if the Closing shall not have occurred on or before the Outside Date (February 28, 2026); *provided* that the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(b) shall not be available to any Party whose breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement set forth in this Agreement has been the primary cause of, or has primarily resulted in, the failure of the Closing to occur on or before the Outside Date;
678: 
679: **(c)** by either Buyer or Seller, by written notice to the other Party, if any Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any final and non-appealable Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action that permanently restrains, enjoins, or otherwise prohibits the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement;

681: **(d)** by Buyer, by written notice to Seller, if there shall have been a breach by Seller of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement that would cause the conditions set forth in Section 7.02(a) or Section 7.02(b) not to be satisfied, and such breach shall not have been cured by Seller within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice of such breach from Buyer (or, if earlier, by the Outside Date); *provided* that Buyer shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(d) if Buyer is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement; or

683: **(e)** by Seller, by written notice to Buyer, if there shall have been a breach by Buyer of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement that would cause the conditions set forth in Section 7.03(a) or Section 7.03(b) not to be satisfied, and such breach shall not have been cured by Buyer within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice of such breach from Seller (or, if earlier, by the Outside Date); *provided* that Seller shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(e) if Seller is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement.

686:

695: **[INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

697: **Section 9.01 Survival**

699: **(a)** The Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until the date that is sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby (giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof).

703: **(c)** All covenants and agreements of the Parties contained in this Agreement that by their terms are to be performed in whole or in part after the Closing shall survive the Closing in accordance with their terms. All covenants and agreements of the Parties that are to be performed in whole prior to or at the Closing shall survive the Closing for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date.

705: **(d)** No claim for indemnification under this Article IX may be asserted by any Buyer Indemnitee or Seller Indemnitee after the expiration of the applicable survival period set forth in this Section 9.01; *provided* that any claim for indemnification that is properly asserted in writing in accordance with Section 9.05 prior to the expiration of the applicable survival period shall survive such expiration until such claim has been finally resolved.

708: 
709: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Article IX, from and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its Affiliates (including, following the Closing, the Company) and their respective directors, officers, employees, managers, members, partners, agents, and Representatives (collectively, the \"Buyer Indemnitees\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or sustained by, or imposed upon, any Buyer Indemnitee arising out of or resulting from:

724:

728:

731: **(b)** *Cap.* The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap (\$43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

lines.text: **Section 7.01 Conditions to Each Party\'s Obligations**

The respective obligations of each Party to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by applicable Law, waiver by each Party) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** No Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action (whether temporary, preliminary, or permanent) that is then in effect and that has the effect of making the transactions contemplated by this Agreement illegal or otherwise preventing or prohibiting the consummation of such transactions.
**(b)** The applicable waiting period (and any extension thereof) under the HSR Act in respect of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall have expired or been terminated.

**(c)** No Action by any Governmental Authority shall be pending that seeks to (i) restrain, enjoin, prevent, prohibit, or make illegal the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (ii) impose limitations on the ability of Buyer to effectively exercise full rights of ownership of the Shares, or (iii) compel Buyer or any of its Affiliates to dispose of or hold separate all or a material portion of the business or assets of the Company.
**Section 7.02 Conditions to Buyer\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Buyer) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* (i) The Fundamental Representations of Seller shall be true and correct in all respects (other than de minimis inaccuracies) as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date, in which case such representation or warranty shall be true and correct as of such earlier date); and (ii) each other representation and warranty of Seller and the Company contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" or \"Material Adverse Effect\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except, in the case of this clause (ii), where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

**(b)** *Covenants.* Seller shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Seller under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.

**(c)** *No Material Adverse Effect.* Since the date of this Agreement, no event, change, effect, development, condition, or occurrence shall have occurred that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

**(d)** *Officer\'s Certificate.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer a certificate, signed by a duly authorized officer of Seller, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Sections 7.02(a), 7.02(b), and 7.02(c) have been satisfied.
**(e)** *Seller Deliverables.* Seller shall have delivered to Buyer all of the closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(a).
**(f)** *Third-Party Consents.* All consents, waivers, approvals, and authorizations set forth on Schedule 4.05 shall have been obtained and shall be in full force and effect.
**(g)** *Escrow Agreement.* The Escrow Agreement shall have been duly executed and delivered by Seller and the Escrow Agent.
**Section 7.03 Conditions to Seller\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Seller) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* Each representation and warranty of Buyer contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to prevent or materially delay the ability of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.

**(b)** *Covenants.* Buyer shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Buyer under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.
**(c)** *Closing Payments.* Buyer shall have delivered the Closing Payment to Seller and the Escrow Amount to the Escrow Agent in accordance with Section 2.03.

**(d)** *Officer\'s Certificate.* Buyer shall have delivered to Seller a certificate, signed by a duly authorized officer or manager of Buyer, dated as of the Closing Date, certifying that the conditions set forth in Sections 7.03(a) and 7.03(b) have been satisfied.
**(e)** *Buyer Deliverables.* Buyer shall have delivered to Seller all of the closing deliverables set forth in Section 2.08(b).
**[ARTICLE VIII]{.underline}**
**[TERMINATION]{.underline}**
**Section 8.01 Termination**
This Agreement may be terminated at any time prior to the Closing:
**(a)** by the mutual written consent of Buyer and Seller;

**(b)** by either Buyer or Seller, by written notice to the other Party, if the Closing shall not have occurred on or before the Outside Date (February 28, 2026); *provided* that the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(b) shall not be available to any Party whose breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement set forth in this Agreement has been the primary cause of, or has primarily resulted in, the failure of the Closing to occur on or before the Outside Date;

**(c)** by either Buyer or Seller, by written notice to the other Party, if any Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any final and non-appealable Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action that permanently restrains, enjoins, or otherwise prohibits the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement;

**(d)** by Buyer, by written notice to Seller, if there shall have been a breach by Seller of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement that would cause the conditions set forth in Section 7.02(a) or Section 7.02(b) not to be satisfied, and such breach shall not have been cured by Seller within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice of such breach from Buyer (or, if earlier, by the Outside Date); *provided* that Buyer shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(d) if Buyer is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement; or

**(e)** by Seller, by written notice to Buyer, if there shall have been a breach by Buyer of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement that would cause the conditions set forth in Section 7.03(a) or Section 7.03(b) not to be satisfied, and such breach shall not have been cured by Buyer within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice of such breach from Seller (or, if earlier, by the Outside Date); *provided* that Seller shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement under this Section 8.01(e) if Seller is then in material breach of any representation, warranty, covenant, or agreement contained in this Agreement.
**Section 8.02 Effect of Termination**

In the event of the termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 8.01, this Agreement shall forthwith become void and have no effect, without any liability on the part of any Party or its respective Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, stockholders, members, managers, partners, agents, or Representatives, and all rights and obligations of the Parties hereunder shall cease; *provided*, *however*, that (a) nothing herein shall relieve any Party from liability for any willful and material breach of this Agreement occurring prior to such termination or for fraud; and (b) the provisions of Section 6.03 (Confidentiality), Section 6.06 (Public Announcements), Section 8.02 (Effect of Termination), Section 8.03 (Expenses), and Article X (Miscellaneous) shall survive any termination of this Agreement and shall remain in full force and effect.
**Section 8.03 Expenses**

Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement (including with respect to HSR Act filing fees, which shall be paid by Buyer pursuant to Section 6.04(c), and Transfer Taxes, which shall be allocated pursuant to Section 6.07(c)), all costs, fees, and expenses (including attorneys\' fees, accountants\' fees, financial advisory fees, and other professional fees and expenses) incurred by or on behalf of a Party in connection with this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby shall be paid by the Party incurring such costs, fees, and expenses, whether or not the transactions contemplated by this Agreement are consummated.
**[ARTICLE IX]{.underline}**
**[INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
**Section 9.01 Survival**

**(a)** The Fundamental Representations shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect until the date that is sixty (60) days following the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations relating to the matters covered thereby (giving effect to any waiver, mitigation, or extension thereof).

**(b)** All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing and continue in full force and effect for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date, and shall thereupon expire and be of no further force or effect.

**(c)** All covenants and agreements of the Parties contained in this Agreement that by their terms are to be performed in whole or in part after the Closing shall survive the Closing in accordance with their terms. All covenants and agreements of the Parties that are to be performed in whole prior to or at the Closing shall survive the Closing for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date.

**(d)** No claim for indemnification under this Article IX may be asserted by any Buyer Indemnitee or Seller Indemnitee after the expiration of the applicable survival period set forth in this Section 9.01; *provided* that any claim for indemnification that is properly asserted in writing in accordance with Section 9.05 prior to the expiration of the applicable survival period shall survive such expiration until such claim has been finally resolved.
**Section 9.02 Indemnification by Seller**

Subject to the terms and conditions of this Article IX, from and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Buyer and its Affiliates (including, following the Closing, the Company) and their respective directors, officers, employees, managers, members, partners, agents, and Representatives (collectively, the \"Buyer Indemnitees\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or sustained by, or imposed upon, any Buyer Indemnitee arising out of or resulting from:

**(a)** any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller contained in Article III or any representation or warranty regarding the Company contained in Article IV (determined, for purposes of calculating Losses only, without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality,\" \"Material Adverse Effect,\" or similar qualification contained therein);
**(b)** any breach or nonperformance of any covenant or agreement of Seller contained in this Agreement;

**(c)** any Transaction Expenses that are not paid prior to or at the Closing to the extent such Transaction Expenses were not included in the calculation of the Purchase Price as finally determined pursuant to Section 2.04; or

**(d)** any Pre-Closing Taxes (meaning all Taxes of the Company attributable to any taxable period ending on or before the Closing Date, or, with respect to any Straddle Period, the Pre-Closing Straddle Amount, in each case to the extent such Taxes were not reflected in the calculation of Closing Indebtedness or Net Working Capital).
**Section 9.03 Indemnification by Buyer**

Subject to the terms and conditions of this Article IX, from and after the Closing, Buyer shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Seller and its Affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees, managers, members, partners, agents, and Representatives (collectively, the \"Seller Indemnitees\") from and against any and all Losses incurred or sustained by, or imposed upon, any Seller Indemnitee arising out of or resulting from:
**(a)** any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Buyer contained in Article V; or
**(b)** any breach or nonperformance of any covenant or agreement of Buyer contained in this Agreement.
**Section 9.04 Limitations on Indemnification**

**(a)** *Basket.* Seller shall not be obligated to indemnify any Buyer Indemnitee for Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) until the aggregate amount of all such Losses exceeds the Basket Amount (\$2,150,000), and then only for Losses in excess of the Basket Amount (it being understood and agreed that the Basket Amount shall operate as a true deductible and not as a \"tipping\" or \"first-dollar\" basket).

**(b)** *Cap.* The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a) (other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap (\$43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value.

**(c)** *Fundamental Representations.* The limitations set forth in Sections 9.04(a) and 9.04(b) shall not apply to Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations. The aggregate liability of Seller for Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations shall not exceed the Purchase Price (as finally determined pursuant to Section 2.04).

**(d)** *Escrow as Source of Recovery.* With respect to claims for indemnification under Section 9.02(a) (other than claims arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations), the Escrow Fund shall be the sole and exclusive source of recovery for all Losses up to the Escrow Amount (\$16,125,000). Claims for Losses under Section 9.02(a) (other than claims arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations) in excess of the Escrow Amount may be pursued directly against Seller, subject in all cases to the Indemnification Cap and the other limitations set forth in this Section 9.04.

**(e)** *Insurance Offset.* The amount of any Losses subject to indemnification under this Article IX shall be reduced by the amount of any insurance proceeds actually received by the indemnified party (net of any costs of collection and any increases in premiums directly attributable to such claim) with respect to such Losses. Each indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to recover under applicable insurance policies for any Losses for which it seeks indemnification hereunder.

**(f)** *Tax Benefits.* The amount of any Losses subject to indemnification under this Article IX shall be reduced by the amount of any Tax benefit actually realized (through a reduction of cash Taxes payable) by the indemnified party or its Affiliates in the taxable year in which such Losses are incurred or in the immediately succeeding taxable year.

**(g)** *Mitigation.* Each indemnified party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate any Losses for which indemnification may be sought under this Article IX. No indemnifying party shall be liable for any Losses that the indemnified party could reasonably have avoided or mitigated.

**(h)** *No Duplication.* No indemnified party shall be entitled to recover the same Losses more than once under multiple provisions of this Agreement or any other Transaction Document.
