add_issue(7, 'General indemnification cap — conform to 12.5% term-sheet cap', 'HIGH', 'Seller SPA §1.01 “Indemnification Cap”; §9.04(b); Term Sheet §8; Buyer Playbook §5.1; Partner Instructions ¶5',

'The draft defines the Indemnification Cap as $43,000,000 (20% of enterprise value) and repeats that amount in §9.04(b). The executed term sheet unambiguously fixes the general cap at 12.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, or $26,875,000. The cap is a binding economic term.',

'“Indemnification Cap” means Forty-Three Million Dollars ($43,000,000), which is equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Base Enterprise Value. Section 9.04(b) provides that Seller’s aggregate liability shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap ($43,000,000).',
'Replace the definition of “Indemnification Cap” in Section 1.01 with:

“Indemnification Cap” means Twenty-Six Million Eight Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars ($26,875,000), which is equal to twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value ($215,000,000 × 0.125).
Replace Section 9.04(b) with:

(b) Cap. The aggregate liability of Seller for all Losses arising under Section 9.02(a), other than Losses arising from breaches of Fundamental Representations or the Special Indemnity, shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap, equal to $26,875,000, which is twelve and one-half percent (12.5%) of the Base Enterprise Value. For the avoidance of doubt, the Escrow Amount of $16,125,000 is a source of recovery and does not limit Buyer’s right to recover up to the Indemnification Cap.',

'This is not a drafting compromise: the term sheet states both the percentage and the dollar amount and makes the cap a binding provision. The proposed language also preserves the agreed $16,125,000 escrow (7.5% of enterprise value) with Pinnacle Trust Company and clarifies that escrow is not itself a recovery cap. See Term Sheet §§4 and 8, Buyer Playbook §5.1.' )

add_issue(8, 'Environmental representation survival — minimum 36 months; longer alternative reserved', 'HIGH', 'Seller SPA §9.01(b); Term Sheet §8; Buyer Playbook §4.2; DD Memo §§III, IV, V; Partner Instructions ¶6',

'The draft gives all non-Fundamental representations only 12 months, without a separate environmental category. That period is inadequate for Dalton Creek, the 24–36 month Hargrove project, delayed regulatory action, and environmental risks that may not become apparent within a year. The current buyer markup should use 36 months, while reserving the option to seek the full applicable statute-of-limitations period.',

'“All representations and warranties contained in this Agreement (other than the Fundamental Representations) shall survive the Closing ... for a period of twelve (12) months following the Closing Date.”',
'Replace Section 9.01(b) and add new Sections 9.01(c)–(e) as follows:

(b) General Representations. All representations and warranties other than Fundamental Representations, Tax Representations, Environmental Representations, and Special Indemnities shall survive the Closing until the date that is eighteen (18) months after the Closing Date.

(c) Environmental Representations. The representations and warranties in Section 4.15 and any other representation or warranty to the extent relating to Environmental Laws, Environmental Permits, Hazardous Substances, Releases, environmental compliance, environmental liabilities, remediation obligations, environmental insurance, CERCLA, RCRA, or environmental proceedings (collectively, the “Environmental Representations”) shall survive the Closing until the date that is thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date.

(d) Covenants. Covenants and agreements to be performed after the Closing shall survive in accordance with their terms. Covenants and agreements to be performed before or at the Closing shall survive for twelve (12) months after the Closing Date, unless a longer period is specified in this Agreement.
(e) Special Indemnities. The Special Indemnity shall survive as provided in Section 9.02(e).
No claim for indemnification may be asserted after the applicable survival period; provided that a claim properly asserted in writing before expiration shall survive until final resolution.',

'The term sheet sets 18 months for general non-Fundamental representations and at least 36 months for environmental representations. The DD memo explains that CERCLA matters can take years to crystallize and that Hargrove continues for 24–36 months. For now, 36 months is the instructed position. Elena should discuss with Marcus whether to seek survival through the full applicable statute of limitations, particularly for CERCLA-related claims. See Term Sheet §8, Buyer Playbook §4.2, DD Memo §§III–V, and Partner Instructions ¶6.' )
add_issue(9, 'Dalton Creek Special Indemnity and escrow holdback', 'HIGH', 'Seller SPA §§9.02, 9.04, 9.08, Exhibit A; Term Sheet §§4, 8, 9; Buyer Playbook §6; DD Memo §III; Partner Instructions ¶7',

'The seller’s draft treats the pending Dalton Creek EPA information request only as a scheduled environmental matter and provides no indemnity specifically covering the known exposure. The DD memo estimates $1,500,000–$6,000,000 of potential CERCLA liability and notes that the matter may not crystallize for years. The term sheet expressly requires a Special Indemnity with 72-month survival, no basket or general cap, and 36-month escrow availability.',

'Section 9.02 provides only general indemnity for breaches of representations, covenants, transaction expenses, and pre-closing taxes. Section 9.08(b) holds pending escrow claims relating to Fundamental Representations through 36 months but does not mention a Special Indemnity. Exhibit A likewise refers only to Fundamental Representation pending claims.',
'Add the following as new Section 9.02(e) (and conform cross-references throughout Article IX):

(e) Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. From and after the Closing, Seller shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Buyer Indemnitees from and against any and all Losses arising out of, resulting from, or relating to (i) the pending information request issued by the United States Environmental Protection Agency under Section 104(e) of CERCLA concerning the Company’s former operations at the Dalton Creek disposal facility located in Clackamas County, Oregon, (ii) any investigation, notice of potential responsibility, enforcement action, administrative order, consent decree, claim, contribution action, cost-recovery action, proceeding, or other governmental or third-party matter relating to the Dalton Creek facility or the Company’s operations there, and (iii) any investigation, assessment, response, removal, remediation, cleanup, natural-resource-damage, defense, settlement, judgment, penalty, fine, or other liability arising from or relating to the Company’s historical handling, treatment, transportation, arranging for disposal, or disposal of Hazardous Substances at the Dalton Creek facility.

The Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall survive the Closing until the date that is seventy-two (72) months after the Closing Date. It shall not be subject to the Basket Amount, the Indemnification Cap, or any other general limitation applicable to claims under Section 9.02(a), and Losses recovered under this Section 9.02(e) shall not reduce the Indemnification Cap or be counted toward the Basket Amount. Buyer shall not be required to first pursue any insurance recovery as a condition to Seller’s obligations, but Buyer shall not recover the same Loss twice.
Revise Section 9.08(b) to read:

(b) Fundamental Representations and Special Indemnity Claims. The portion of the Escrow Fund allocated to claims relating to Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be held until the date that is thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date, less amounts subject to pending and unresolved claims properly asserted before that date. After the applicable claim is finally resolved, the Escrow Agent shall release to Buyer the amount finally determined to be payable and release any excess reserve to Seller. Buyer’s right to pursue the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity directly against Seller after the 36-month escrow holdback expires, and through the 72-month survival period, shall not be limited by the release of the escrow.
Conform Exhibit A so that the escrow agreement expressly provides for a 36-month holdback for amounts allocated to Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity.',

'This is a required deal-term implementation, not a new economic ask. A disclosed matter may not constitute a breach of a representation, and a 12- or 36-month general survival period does not protect against a CERCLA claim that crystallizes later. The Special Indemnity should be dollar-one, outside the general cap and basket, survive 72 months, and use the escrow as a source of recovery for 36 months. The DD memo also notes that Dalton Creek insurance coverage may be excluded or uncertain, so the indemnity should not be conditioned on exhausting insurance. See Term Sheet §§4, 8, 9; Buyer Playbook §6; DD Memo §III; Partner Instructions ¶7.' )
add_issue(10, 'Pro-sandbagging — replace Section 9.06', 'CRITICAL', 'Seller SPA §9.06; Buyer Playbook §5.3; Partner Instructions ¶2',

'The draft’s express anti-sandbagging sentence would bar Buyer from recovering for a breach known to Buyer or its Representatives as of closing. That would penalize Whitmore for conducting the extensive financial, legal, regulatory, and environmental diligence contemplated by the deal and could eliminate recourse for known issues, including Dalton Creek, if the facts also constitute a breach of a representation.',

'“Buyer shall not be entitled to indemnification under this Article IX with respect to any breach or inaccuracy of any representation or warranty of Seller or the Company of which Buyer or any of its Representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.”',
'Delete Section 9.06 in its entirety and replace it with:

Section 9.06 Effect of Investigation and Knowledge. The right of Buyer and the other Buyer Indemnitees to indemnification or any other remedy based on the representations, warranties, covenants, and obligations set forth in this Agreement shall not be affected, limited, diminished, or otherwise impaired by any investigation conducted by or on behalf of Buyer or any knowledge acquired, or capable of being acquired, by Buyer or any of its Representatives at any time, whether before or after the execution and delivery of this Agreement or before or after the Closing Date, with respect to the accuracy or inaccuracy of, or compliance with, any representation, warranty, covenant, or obligation. No claim for indemnification shall be defeated or reduced by reason of any investigation, knowledge, notice, or information available to or obtained by Buyer or any of its Representatives, regardless of when obtained.',

'An affirmative pro-sandbagging provision is mandatory under the playbook and is especially important in a PE acquisition with extensive diligence. The contractual representations allocate risk independently of what Buyer discovers. Delaware law does not supply a clear default rule, so the SPA must state the intended allocation expressly. See Buyer Playbook §5.3 and Partner Instructions ¶2.' )

add_issue(11, 'R&W Insurance subrogation waiver', 'MEDIUM', 'Seller SPA Article IX/Article X; Term Sheet §10; Buyer Playbook §8.2; Partner Instructions ¶11',

'The draft contains no reference to Whitmore’s contemplated Granite Ridge Underwriters R&W policy and no waiver of the insurer’s subrogation rights. The term sheet expressly requires Buyer to cause the insurer to waive recovery against Seller and related persons except for Seller fraud.',
'No provision in the seller’s draft addresses R&W Insurance or the insurer’s subrogation rights against Seller or Seller-related persons.',
'Insert new Section 10.13 immediately before Section 10.12 (and renumber succeeding sections):

Section 10.13 R&W Insurance; Subrogation Waiver. Buyer shall obtain and maintain a representations and warranties insurance policy in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement (the “R&W Insurance Policy”) and shall cause the R&W Insurance Policy to provide that the insurer shall irrevocably waive, and shall not exercise or pursue, any right of subrogation or other right of recovery against Seller or any of its Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents, or Representatives with respect to any claim made by Buyer or any Buyer Indemnitee under the R&W Insurance Policy, except to the extent the applicable Loss arises from or relates to actual fraud committed by Seller. Buyer shall not amend, modify, waive, or terminate any provision of the R&W Insurance Policy in a manner that would adversely affect Seller’s rights under this Section 10.13 without Seller’s prior written consent.',

'This implements the term-sheet commitment and the market-standard protection expected in a buy-side R&W insurance structure. It does not reduce Seller’s SPA indemnity, the $26,875,000 general cap, the escrow, or the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity. See Term Sheet §10, Buyer Playbook §8.2, and Partner Instructions ¶11.' )
add_issue(12, 'Non-compete — conform duration, geography, and business scope', 'MEDIUM', 'Seller SPA §6.09(a); Term Sheet §11; Buyer Playbook §10.1; Partner Instructions ¶12',

'The draft restricts Seller and all Affiliates for five years, throughout the United States, from being connected with “any business.” That would sweep in Evergreen’s unrelated construction and timber operations and creates avoidable enforceability risk. The term sheet fixes a three-year restriction limited to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada.',

'“For a period of five (5) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, control, participate in, consult with, render services for, or in any manner be connected with any business anywhere in the United States.”',
'Replace Section 6.09(a) with:

(a) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller and its controlled Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, financing, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, in each case in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada and to the extent such services are the same as or substantially similar to the services conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict (i) Seller’s or its Affiliates’ existing construction and timber operations as conducted as of the Closing Date; (ii) passive ownership of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity; (iii) environmental-related activities incidental to, and performed solely in connection with, Seller’s construction or timber operations; or (iv) any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation or hazardous waste management services as of the Closing Date.

For consistency with the executed term sheet, replace the first sentence of Section 6.09(b) with: “For a period of two (2) years following the Closing Date, Seller and its Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce or attempt to induce any such employee to terminate employment with the Company.” Retain the customary general-solicitation and employee-initiated-contact carve-outs. The customer/supplier non-solicitation language in the seller draft is not part of the term-sheet formulation and should be removed unless Marcus directs that it be retained as an additional buyer protection.',

'The proposed language tracks the term sheet exactly and follows the playbook’s reasonableness guidance. A nationwide “any business” prohibition is particularly problematic for a diversified seller with construction and timber operations and could be struck as overbroad. The non-solicitation duration should also be conformed to the term sheet’s two-year employee-only formulation unless the client affirmatively elects to preserve the draft’s additional customer/supplier restriction. See Term Sheet §11, Buyer Playbook §10.1, and Partner Instructions ¶12.' )

(d) Buyer’s Operating Flexibility. Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05 shall restrict Buyer’s right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer’s sole discretion, including making capital-expenditure decisions, pricing changes, personnel decisions, strategic investments, acquisitions, dispositions, organizational restructurings, and operational modifications. No such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05 unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of capital expenditures or employees, or refrain from diverting or redirecting business opportunities, except to the extent an action is taken with that primary purpose.

(e) Payment. Any Earnout Payment finally determined to be payable shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within sixty (60) days after the end of the Measurement Period; provided that, if the amount is not finally determined by that date because Seller timely disputed Buyer’s calculation, Buyer shall pay the finally determined amount within five (5) Business Days after final determination. The parties shall treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price for U.S. federal income tax purposes.',
    'The $25,000,000 maximum, $38,000,000 full-payment threshold, $32,000,000 floor, linear interpolation, and December 31, 2026 measurement period are agreed economic terms and should be retained. The draft’s affirmative “maximize” and past-practice obligations would give Seller a de facto veto over Whitmore’s platform integration, bolt-on acquisitions, restructuring, and operational improvements. The replacement is the only acceptable playbook formulation: a narrow negative covenant keyed to primary purpose. See Term Sheet §5, Buyer Playbook §7.2, and Partner Instructions ¶3.' )

(b) Fundamental Representations and Special Indemnity Claims. The portion of the Escrow Fund allocated to claims relating to Fundamental Representations and the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity shall be held until the date that is thirty-six (36) months after the Closing Date, less amounts subject to pending and unresolved claims properly asserted before that date. After the applicable claim is finally resolved, the Escrow Agent shall release to Buyer the amount finally determined to be payable and release any excess reserve to Seller. (a) Non-Competition. For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller and its controlled Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, engage in, own, manage, operate, finance, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, financing, or control of any business engaged in the provision of environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services, in each case in the States of Oregon, Washington, California, or Nevada and to the extent such services are the same as or substantially similar to the services conducted by the Company as of the Closing Date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Section 6.09(a) shall not restrict (i) Seller’s or its Affiliates’ existing construction and timber operations as conducted as of the Closing Date; (ii) passive ownership of less than five percent (5%) of the outstanding equity securities of any publicly traded entity; (iii) environmental-related activities incidental to, and performed solely in connection with, Seller’s construction or timber operations; or (iv) any portfolio company or operating subsidiary of Seller that is not engaged in environmental remediation or hazardous waste management services as of the Closing Date.

For consistency with the executed term sheet, replace the first sentence of Section 6.09(b) with: “For a period of two (2) years following the Closing Date, Seller and its Affiliates shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or engage any individual who is an employee of the Company as of the Closing Date, or induce or attempt to induce any such employee to terminate employment with the Company.” Retain the customary general-solicitation and employee-initiated-contact carve-outs. The customer/supplier non-solicitation language in the seller draft is not part of the term-sheet formulation and should be removed unless Marcus directs that it be retained as an additional buyer protection.',
    'The proposed language tracks the term sheet exactly and follows the playbook’s reasonableness guidance. A nationwide “any business” prohibition is particularly problematic for a diversified seller with construction and timber operations and could be struck as overbroad. The non-solicitation duration should also be conformed to the term sheet’s two-year employee-only formulation unless the client affirmatively elects to preserve the draft’s additional customer/supplier restriction. See Term Sheet §11, Buyer Playbook §10.1, and Partner Instructions ¶12.""")

1: **SPA MARKUP MEMORANDUM**
2: 
3: **Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**
4: 
5: *Review of Seller's Draft Stock Purchase Agreement*
6: 
7:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8:   **Prepared for**                    Whitmore Capital Partners LLC
9:   ----------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10:   **Prepared by**                     Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP --- Buyer's counsel
11: 
12:   **Review date**                     October 29, 2025
13: 
14:   **Transaction**                     Acquisition of 100% of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. from Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.
15: 
16:   **Status**                          Buyer-side markup memorandum; draft-ready replacement language
17:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
18: 
19: > **PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**
20: >
21: > *This memorandum is prepared solely for Whitmore Capital Partners LLC and its advisers in connection with the proposed acquisition. It is not intended for distribution to the seller or any other person.*
22: 
23: # Executive Summary
24: 
25: The seller's initial SPA is materially seller-favorable and departs from the executed September 10, 2025 term sheet and buyer playbook on several agreed or non-negotiable protections. The most important changes are to preserve the buyer's MAE and indemnification protections, remove the anti-sandbagging and affirmative earnout-operating obligations, and address the known environmental and government-contract risks identified in diligence.
26: 
27:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
28:   **Priority**      **Issue**                                                **SPA location**          **Recommended action**
29:   ----------------- -------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
30:   CRITICAL          MAE carve-outs lack disproportionate-impact qualifiers   §1.01 definition          Replace definition carve-outs; do not accept carve-outs that neutralize regulatory/industry risk.
31: 
32:   CRITICAL          Anti-sandbagging                                         §9.06                     Strike in full; insert affirmative pro-sandbagging language.
33: 
34:   CRITICAL          Earnout operating covenant                               §2.05(d)                  Replace with primary-purpose negative covenant; conform timing and mechanics to term sheet.
35: 
36:   CRITICAL          Government contract novation/recognition                 §§4.16, 6.05, 7.02        Add specific reps, pre-/post-closing cooperation, and a balanced submission/no-denial closing condition.
37: 
38:   HIGH              General indemnification cap is 20% rather than 12.5%     §1.01; §9.04(b)           Change \$43,000,000 to \$26,875,000; retain \$16,125,000 Pinnacle escrow and 18-/36-month release mechanics.
39: 
40:   HIGH              Environmental rep survival is 12 months                  §9.01                     Carve environmental reps out and give them 36-month survival; flag full-statute alternative.
41: 
42:   HIGH              No Dalton Creek Special Indemnity                        §9.02; §9.08; Exhibit A   Add 72-month, dollar-one, uncapped Special Indemnity; hold the designated escrow portion for 36 months.
43: 
44:   HIGH              No interim affiliate-transaction restriction             §6.01                     Add buyer-consent restriction covering new, amended, extended, renewed, paid, or terminated affiliate dealings.
45: 
46:   HIGH              Debt repayment is "at or promptly following" closing     §2.03(d); §7.02           Require payoff letters at least three business days before closing and simultaneous funds-flow payoff.
47: 
48:   MEDIUM            No environmental permit change-of-control cooperation    §4.15; §6.05; §7.02       Add OR/WA/CA/NV notification/approval cooperation through at least 12 months post-closing.
49: 
50:   MEDIUM            No R&W insurer subrogation waiver                        Article IX/Article X      Add Granite Ridge waiver except for Seller fraud.
51: 
52:   MEDIUM            Non-compete is 5 years/nationwide/any business           §6.09                     Conform to 3 years; OR/WA/CA/NV; environmental remediation and hazardous waste management only.
53:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
54: 
55: The memo also identifies schedule and drafting discrepancies that should be corrected before circulation, including inconsistent Dalton Creek facts, inconsistent environmental insurance policy numbers, and a confidentiality-agreement date mismatch.
56: 
57: # Materials Reviewed and Methodology
58: 
59: - **Seller's draft SPA.** Initial draft circulated by Douglas Renwick on October 22, 2025, including disclosure schedules and exhibits.
60: 
61: - **Executed term sheet.** Binding term sheet dated September 10, 2025; used as the primary benchmark for economic terms and agreed restrictive covenants.
62: 
63: - **Buyer M&A Playbook.** Environmental services sector playbook, version 4.2 (October 2025); used for mandatory buyer positions and sector-specific drafting.
64: 
65: - **Environmental DD memo.** Environmental Practice Group summary; used to identify Dalton Creek, Hargrove, permits, government contracts, and insurance risks.
66: 
67: - **Partner instructions.** Elena Vasquez-Moreno's markup instructions; used to prioritize issues and identify positions reserved for discussion with Marcus Devereaux.
68: 
69: Each issue below is organized by SPA article/section and includes: (i) the seller's relevant language or identified omission; (ii) full buyer replacement language intended to be inserted into the SPA; (iii) a track-changes-style rationale; and (iv) a priority and source cross-reference.
70: 
71: # Article I --- Definitions
72: 
73: ## **1. MAE definition --- disproportionate-impact qualifiers**
74: 
75: **PRIORITY: CRITICAL \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §1.01; Buyer Playbook §§2.1--2.2; Partner Instructions ¶1*
76: 
77: **Issue summary.** The seller's definition excludes changes affecting the environmental services industry generally and changes in Environmental Laws without an exception for target-specific or disproportionate harm. Because Cascadia's value is directly exposed to environmental regulation and industry economics, the carve-outs could remove the very risks the MAE condition is intended to address.
78: 
79: **Original seller language.**
80: 
81: > **SELLER DRAFT ---** "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company; provided, however, that none of the following shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law; \[remaining customary carve-outs\].
82: 
83: **Draft-ready buyer language.**
84: 
85: > **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law, other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii); (v) acts of war, armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; or (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period, provided that the underlying facts, circumstances, and causes of any such failure may be considered in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred; provided, further, that any change, effect, event, or development referred to in clauses... (line truncated to 2000 chars)
86: >
87: > **TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The qualifier is a firm-wide, non-negotiable buyer position for environmental services transactions. It preserves customary protection for truly general developments while retaining recourse where a regulatory or industry event hits Cascadia disproportionately. This is especially important because the DD memo identifies active environmental permits, government contracts, and a pending CERCLA information request. See Buyer Playbook §§2.1--2.2 and Partner Instructions ¶1.
88: 
89: # Article II --- Purchase Price and Earnout
90: 
91: ## **2. Earnout mechanics and operational covenant**
92: 
93: **PRIORITY: CRITICAL \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §2.05(a)--(e); Term Sheet §5; Buyer Playbook §§7.1--7.2; Partner Instructions ¶3*
94: 
95: **Issue summary.** The financial thresholds and interpolation formula in the seller's draft match the term sheet, but the timing mechanics do not: the draft allows 60 days for Buyer's calculation and payment within 10 Business Days after final determination, while the term sheet calls for a calculation within 45 days and payment within 60 days after the measurement period. More importantly, §2.05(d) imposes an affirmative obligation to operate consistently with past practice, maximize the earnout, maintain resources, and avoid diversion of opportunities.
96: 
97: **Original seller language.**
98: 
99: > **SELLER DRAFT ---** "From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. \... Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources \... and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates."
100: 
101: **Draft-ready buyer language.**
102: 
103: > **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** Replace Section 2.05 in its entirety with the following:\
104: > \
105: > (a) Maximum Earnout Payment. If the Company's Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period equals or exceeds \$38,000,000, Buyer shall pay Seller \$25,000,000 (the "Maximum Earnout Payment").\
106: > \
107: > (b) Pro-Rata Earnout. If the Company's Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is at least \$32,000,000 but less than \$38,000,000, Buyer shall pay an amount equal to (\$25,000,000 ÷ (\$38,000,000 − \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA − \$32,000,000). If Adjusted EBITDA is less than \$32,000,000, no Earnout Payment shall be payable. The parties acknowledge that the formula provides for linear interpolation of approximately \$4,166,667 for each \$1,000,000 of Adjusted EBITDA above \$32,000,000.\
108: > \
109: > (c) Measurement Period; Calculation. The Measurement Period is the twelve-month period ending December 31, 2026. Within forty-five (45) days after the end of the Measurement Period, Buyer shall deliver to Seller a written calculation of Adjusted EBITDA and the resulting Earnout Payment, together with reasonable supporting detail. Seller shall have thirty (30) days after receipt to deliver a written objection specifying each disputed item. Any dispute shall be resolved under the independent-accountant procedures in Section 2.04, applied mutatis mutandis.\
110: > \
111: > (d) Buyer's Operating Flexibility. Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05 shall restrict Buyer's right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer's sole discretion, including making capital-expenditure decisions, pricing changes, personnel decisions, strategic investments, acquisitions, dispositions, organizational restructurings, and operational modifications. No such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05 unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of capital expenditures or employees, or refrain from diverting or redirecting business opportunities, except to the extent an action is taken with that primary purpose.\
112: > \
113: > (e) Payment. Any Earnout Payment finally determined to be payable shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within sixty (60) days after the end of the Measurement Period; provided that, if the amount is not finally determined by that date because Seller timely disputed Buyer's calculation, Buyer shall pay the finally determined amount within five (5) Business Days after final determination. The parties shall treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
114: >
115: > **TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The \$25,000,000 maximum, \$38,000,000 full-payment threshold, \$32,000,000 floor, linear interpolation, and December 31, 2026 measurement period are agreed economic terms and should be retained. The draft's affirmative "maximize" and past-practice obligations would give Seller a de facto veto over Whitmore's platform integration, bolt-on acquisitions, restructuring, and operational improvements. The replacement is the only acceptable playbook formulation: a narrow negative covenant keyed to primary purpose. See Term Sheet §5, Buyer Playbook §7.2, and Partner Instructions ¶3.
116: 
117: # Article IV --- Representations and Warranties Regarding the Company
118: 
119: ## **3. Government contracts --- novation/recognition, representations, and closing mechanics**
120: 
121: **PRIORITY: CRITICAL \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §4.16; §§6.05, 7.02(f); Term Sheet §§7, 12, 13; Buyer Playbook §12.2 and §13.2(a); DD Memo §VI; Partner Instructions ¶4*
122: 
123: **Issue summary.** The draft identifies four government contracts and represents only that they are in force and not in material default. It does not address the federal Anti-Assignment Act, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, novation/recognition submissions, contracting-officer communications, or the possibility of termination after the change of control. The DD memo identifies the two federal contracts as requiring novation analysis and the four contracts collectively as a material revenue stream.
124: 
125: **Original seller language.**
126: 
127: > **SELLER DRAFT ---** Section 4.16(a) states that the Company is party to four active government contracts with Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management. Section 4.16(b) states only that each is in full force and effect and that the Company is not in material breach or default. Section 6.05 contains only a general commercially reasonable efforts covenant to obtain third-party consents. No provision addresses novation or recognition.
128: 
129: **Draft-ready buyer language.**
130: 
131: > **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** Replace Section 4.16 with the following:\
132: > \
133: > Section 4.16 Government Contracts.\
134: > (a) Schedule 4.16 contains a true, correct, and complete list of each Government Contract, including all amendments, modifications, task orders, statements of work, and other supplements. The Government Contracts include the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality contract, the Washington Department of Ecology contract, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers contract, and the Bureau of Land Management contract.\
135: > (b) Each Government Contract is valid, binding, in full force and effect, and enforceable against the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, the applicable Governmental Authority. The Company is in material compliance with each Government Contract, and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time, would constitute a material breach or default.\
136: > (c) No Government Contract is subject to a pending or, to Seller's Knowledge, threatened termination for default or convenience, suspension, non-renewal, or material modification. No contracting officer or other Governmental Authority has notified the Company or Seller of an intent to terminate, suspend, or materially modify any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.\
137: > (d) Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, or proposed suspension, and no such proceeding is pending or, to Seller's Knowledge, threatened.\
138: > (e) Seller has delivered to Buyer complete copies of all Government Contracts and all related amendments, modifications, task orders, correspondence, notices, and submissions relating to any change-of-control, assignment, novation, recognition, or consent requirement.\
139: > (f) The parties acknowledge that the acquisition may require novation, recognition, or other approval under 41 U.S.C. §6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, including FAR §42.1204, or analogous state procurement requirements.\
140: > \
141: > Insert new Section 6.06A immediately before current Section 6.06 (and renumber subsequent sections):\
142: > \
143: > Section 6.06A Government Contract Novation and Recognition.\
144: > (a) Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, promptly notify each applicable contracting officer and other Governmental Authority of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and, in any event, submit each required novation, recognition, change-of-control, or similar request no later than ten (10) Business Days after the date of this Agreement, or such earlier date as required by applicable Law or contract.\
145: > (b) Seller and the Company shall prepare and submit complete request packages, including the information required under FAR §42.1204 and analogous state requirements, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all required novation agreements, recognition agreements, consents, or written confirmations that interim performance may continue. Seller shall provide Buyer drafts before submission and copies of all submissions, responses, and communications promptly after delivery or receipt.\
146: > (c) From the date of this Agreement through the Closing, Seller shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, withdraw, amend, or materially supplement any submission without Buyer's prior written consent. Following the Closing, Seller shall continue to provide reasonable cooperation, information, signatures, and participation in meetings requested by Buyer in connection with any pending novation or recognition process for at least twelve (12) months.\
147: > \
148: > Add the following to Section 7.02 as a new clause (h):\
149: > (h) Government Contract Status. With respect to each Government Contract for which a novation, recognition, consent, or change-of-control submission is required, (i) the required submission has been made, (ii) the applicable contracting officer has not denied the request or indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, or materially modify the Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, and (iii) Buyer has received written confirmation that interim performance may continue pending final action, if a final novation or recognition agreement has not been executed. Buyer may waive this condition in writing.
150: >
151: > **TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** This is a critical risk allocation issue. The DD memo states that the federal contracts may require novation under FAR §42.1204 and that failure to obtain required novation could result in termination. Given agency timing, the recommended interim position is not to require executed novations as an absolute closing condition; instead require submission of all packages, no denial or termination signal, and written confirmation that interim performance may continue, with a post-closing cooperation tail. Elena should discuss with Marcus whether to push for executed novations as a hard condition or retain this balanced formulation. See DD Memo §§VI.B--C, Buyer Playbook §12.2 and §13.2(a), and Partner Instructions ¶4.
152: 
153: # Article VI --- Covenants
154: 
155: ## **4. Interim affiliate-transaction restriction**
156: 
157: **PRIORITY: HIGH \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §6.01(b); Seller SPA §§4.21, Schedule 4.09, Schedule 4.21; Buyer Playbook §3.2; Partner Instructions ¶8*
158: 
159: **Issue summary.** The interim covenant lists general restrictions but omits an express prohibition on new, amended, extended, renewed, terminated, or paid affiliate transactions. This is material because the Company pays \$1,600,000 annual rent under the Seller-affiliate lease and has disclosed a \$350,000 annual management-services arrangement. Those arrangements can be expanded or accelerated between signing and closing unless expressly restricted.
160: 
161: **Original seller language.**
162: 
163: > **SELLER DRAFT ---** Section 6.01(b) prohibits specified actions, including amendments to material contracts, but contains no specific restriction on transactions with Seller, Seller affiliates, or Seller-related persons. Section 4.21 merely discloses existing affiliate transactions.
164: 
165: **Draft-ready buyer language.**
166: 
167: > **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** Add the following as a new clause (xiv) to Section 6.01(b):\
168: > \
169: > (xiv) directly or indirectly (A) enter into any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, member, shareholder, partner, or family member of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, (B) amend, modify, extend, renew, supplement, or otherwise alter any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with any such Person, (C) make any payment or transfer any asset to any such Person, other than compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, or (D) terminate any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with any such Person, in each case without Buyer's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
170: >

lines.text: **SPA MARKUP MEMORANDUM**
**Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**
*Review of Seller's Draft Stock Purchase Agreement*
**Prepared for**                    Whitmore Capital Partners LLC
**Prepared by**                     Ashford, Pennington & Yates LLP --- Buyer's counsel
**Review date**                     October 29, 2025
**Transaction**                     Acquisition of 100% of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc. from Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.
**Status**                          Buyer-side markup memorandum; draft-ready replacement language
> **PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT**

> *This memorandum is prepared solely for Whitmore Capital Partners LLC and its advisers in connection with the proposed acquisition. It is not intended for distribution to the seller or any other person.*
# Executive Summary

The seller's initial SPA is materially seller-favorable and departs from the executed September 10, 2025 term sheet and buyer playbook on several agreed or non-negotiable protections. The most important changes are to preserve the buyer's MAE and indemnification protections, remove the anti-sandbagging and affirmative earnout-operating obligations, and address the known environmental and government-contract risks identified in diligence.
**Priority**      **Issue**                                                **SPA location**          **Recommended action**
CRITICAL          MAE carve-outs lack disproportionate-impact qualifiers   §1.01 definition          Replace definition carve-outs; do not accept carve-outs that neutralize regulatory/industry risk.
CRITICAL          Anti-sandbagging                                         §9.06                     Strike in full; insert affirmative pro-sandbagging language.
CRITICAL          Earnout operating covenant                               §2.05(d)                  Replace with primary-purpose negative covenant; conform timing and mechanics to term sheet.

CRITICAL          Government contract novation/recognition                 §§4.16, 6.05, 7.02        Add specific reps, pre-/post-closing cooperation, and a balanced submission/no-denial closing condition.

HIGH              General indemnification cap is 20% rather than 12.5%     §1.01; §9.04(b)           Change \$43,000,000 to \$26,875,000; retain \$16,125,000 Pinnacle escrow and 18-/36-month release mechanics.
HIGH              Environmental rep survival is 12 months                  §9.01                     Carve environmental reps out and give them 36-month survival; flag full-statute alternative.

HIGH              No Dalton Creek Special Indemnity                        §9.02; §9.08; Exhibit A   Add 72-month, dollar-one, uncapped Special Indemnity; hold the designated escrow portion for 36 months.

HIGH              No interim affiliate-transaction restriction             §6.01                     Add buyer-consent restriction covering new, amended, extended, renewed, paid, or terminated affiliate dealings.

HIGH              Debt repayment is "at or promptly following" closing     §2.03(d); §7.02           Require payoff letters at least three business days before closing and simultaneous funds-flow payoff.
MEDIUM            No environmental permit change-of-control cooperation    §4.15; §6.05; §7.02       Add OR/WA/CA/NV notification/approval cooperation through at least 12 months post-closing.
MEDIUM            No R&W insurer subrogation waiver                        Article IX/Article X      Add Granite Ridge waiver except for Seller fraud.
MEDIUM            Non-compete is 5 years/nationwide/any business           §6.09                     Conform to 3 years; OR/WA/CA/NV; environmental remediation and hazardous waste management only.

The memo also identifies schedule and drafting discrepancies that should be corrected before circulation, including inconsistent Dalton Creek facts, inconsistent environmental insurance policy numbers, and a confidentiality-agreement date mismatch.
# Materials Reviewed and Methodology
- **Seller's draft SPA.** Initial draft circulated by Douglas Renwick on October 22, 2025, including disclosure schedules and exhibits.
- **Executed term sheet.** Binding term sheet dated September 10, 2025; used as the primary benchmark for economic terms and agreed restrictive covenants.
- **Buyer M&A Playbook.** Environmental services sector playbook, version 4.2 (October 2025); used for mandatory buyer positions and sector-specific drafting.
- **Environmental DD memo.** Environmental Practice Group summary; used to identify Dalton Creek, Hargrove, permits, government contracts, and insurance risks.
- **Partner instructions.** Elena Vasquez-Moreno's markup instructions; used to prioritize issues and identify positions reserved for discussion with Marcus Devereaux.

Each issue below is organized by SPA article/section and includes: (i) the seller's relevant language or identified omission; (ii) full buyer replacement language intended to be inserted into the SPA; (iii) a track-changes-style rationale; and (iv) a priority and source cross-reference.
# Article I --- Definitions
## **1. MAE definition --- disproportionate-impact qualifiers**
**PRIORITY: CRITICAL \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §1.01; Buyer Playbook §§2.1--2.2; Partner Instructions ¶1*

**Issue summary.** The seller's definition excludes changes affecting the environmental services industry generally and changes in Environmental Laws without an exception for target-specific or disproportionate harm. Because Cascadia's value is directly exposed to environmental regulation and industry economics, the carve-outs could remove the very risks the MAE condition is intended to address.
**Original seller language.**

> **SELLER DRAFT ---** "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company; provided, however, that none of the following shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law; \[remaining customary carve-outs\].
**Draft-ready buyer language.**

> **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law, other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii); (v) acts of war, armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornados, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; or (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period, provided that the underlying facts, circumstances, and causes of any such failure may be considered in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred; provided, further, that any change, effect, event, or development referred to in clauses... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

> **TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The qualifier is a firm-wide, non-negotiable buyer position for environmental services transactions. It preserves customary protection for truly general developments while retaining recourse where a regulatory or industry event hits Cascadia disproportionately. This is especially important because the DD memo identifies active environmental permits, government contracts, and a pending CERCLA information request. See Buyer Playbook §§2.1--2.2 and Partner Instructions ¶1.
# Article II --- Purchase Price and Earnout
## **2. Earnout mechanics and operational covenant**
**PRIORITY: CRITICAL \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §2.05(a)--(e); Term Sheet §5; Buyer Playbook §§7.1--7.2; Partner Instructions ¶3*

**Issue summary.** The financial thresholds and interpolation formula in the seller's draft match the term sheet, but the timing mechanics do not: the draft allows 60 days for Buyer's calculation and payment within 10 Business Days after final determination, while the term sheet calls for a calculation within 45 days and payment within 60 days after the measurement period. More importantly, §2.05(d) imposes an affirmative obligation to operate consistently with past practice, maximize the earnout, maintain resources, and avoid diversion of opportunities.
**Original seller language.**

> **SELLER DRAFT ---** "From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. \... Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources \... and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates."
**Draft-ready buyer language.**
> **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** Replace Section 2.05 in its entirety with the following:\
> (a) Maximum Earnout Payment. If the Company's Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period equals or exceeds \$38,000,000, Buyer shall pay Seller \$25,000,000 (the "Maximum Earnout Payment").\

> (b) Pro-Rata Earnout. If the Company's Adjusted EBITDA for the Measurement Period is at least \$32,000,000 but less than \$38,000,000, Buyer shall pay an amount equal to (\$25,000,000 ÷ (\$38,000,000 − \$32,000,000)) × (Actual Adjusted EBITDA − \$32,000,000). If Adjusted EBITDA is less than \$32,000,000, no Earnout Payment shall be payable. The parties acknowledge that the formula provides for linear interpolation of approximately \$4,166,667 for each \$1,000,000 of Adjusted EBITDA above \$32,000,000.\

> (c) Measurement Period; Calculation. The Measurement Period is the twelve-month period ending December 31, 2026. Within forty-five (45) days after the end of the Measurement Period, Buyer shall deliver to Seller a written calculation of Adjusted EBITDA and the resulting Earnout Payment, together with reasonable supporting detail. Seller shall have thirty (30) days after receipt to deliver a written objection specifying each disputed item. Any dispute shall be resolved under the independent-accountant procedures in Section 2.04, applied mutatis mutandis.\

> (d) Buyer's Operating Flexibility. Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05 shall restrict Buyer's right to operate, integrate, restructure, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer's sole discretion, including making capital-expenditure decisions, pricing changes, personnel decisions, strategic investments, acquisitions, dispositions, organizational restructurings, and operational modifications. No such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05 unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. Buyer shall have no obligation to maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of capital expenditures or employees, or refrain from diverting or redirecting business opportunities, except to the extent an action is taken with that primary purpose.\

> (e) Payment. Any Earnout Payment finally determined to be payable shall be paid by Buyer to Seller within sixty (60) days after the end of the Measurement Period; provided that, if the amount is not finally determined by that date because Seller timely disputed Buyer's calculation, Buyer shall pay the finally determined amount within five (5) Business Days after final determination. The parties shall treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price for U.S. federal income tax purposes.

> **TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The \$25,000,000 maximum, \$38,000,000 full-payment threshold, \$32,000,000 floor, linear interpolation, and December 31, 2026 measurement period are agreed economic terms and should be retained. The draft's affirmative "maximize" and past-practice obligations would give Seller a de facto veto over Whitmore's platform integration, bolt-on acquisitions, restructuring, and operational improvements. The replacement is the only acceptable playbook formulation: a narrow negative covenant keyed to primary purpose. See Term Sheet §5, Buyer Playbook §7.2, and Partner Instructions ¶3.
# Article IV --- Representations and Warranties Regarding the Company
## **3. Government contracts --- novation/recognition, representations, and closing mechanics**
**PRIORITY: CRITICAL \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §4.16; §§6.05, 7.02(f); Term Sheet §§7, 12, 13; Buyer Playbook §12.2 and §13.2(a); DD Memo §VI; Partner Instructions ¶4*

**Issue summary.** The draft identifies four government contracts and represents only that they are in force and not in material default. It does not address the federal Anti-Assignment Act, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, novation/recognition submissions, contracting-officer communications, or the possibility of termination after the change of control. The DD memo identifies the two federal contracts as requiring novation analysis and the four contracts collectively as a material revenue stream.
**Original seller language.**

> **SELLER DRAFT ---** Section 4.16(a) states that the Company is party to four active government contracts with Oregon DEQ, Washington Ecology, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management. Section 4.16(b) states only that each is in full force and effect and that the Company is not in material breach or default. Section 6.05 contains only a general commercially reasonable efforts covenant to obtain third-party consents. No provision addresses novation or recognition.
**Draft-ready buyer language.**
> **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** Replace Section 4.16 with the following:\
> Section 4.16 Government Contracts.\

> (a) Schedule 4.16 contains a true, correct, and complete list of each Government Contract, including all amendments, modifications, task orders, statements of work, and other supplements. The Government Contracts include the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality contract, the Washington Department of Ecology contract, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers contract, and the Bureau of Land Management contract.\

> (b) Each Government Contract is valid, binding, in full force and effect, and enforceable against the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, the applicable Governmental Authority. The Company is in material compliance with each Government Contract, and no event has occurred that, with notice or lapse of time, would constitute a material breach or default.\

> (c) No Government Contract is subject to a pending or, to Seller's Knowledge, threatened termination for default or convenience, suspension, non-renewal, or material modification. No contracting officer or other Governmental Authority has notified the Company or Seller of an intent to terminate, suspend, or materially modify any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.\

> (d) Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, or proposed suspension, and no such proceeding is pending or, to Seller's Knowledge, threatened.\

> (e) Seller has delivered to Buyer complete copies of all Government Contracts and all related amendments, modifications, task orders, correspondence, notices, and submissions relating to any change-of-control, assignment, novation, recognition, or consent requirement.\

> (f) The parties acknowledge that the acquisition may require novation, recognition, or other approval under 41 U.S.C. §6305, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, including FAR §42.1204, or analogous state procurement requirements.\
> Insert new Section 6.06A immediately before current Section 6.06 (and renumber subsequent sections):\
> Section 6.06A Government Contract Novation and Recognition.\

> (a) Seller shall, and shall cause the Company to, promptly notify each applicable contracting officer and other Governmental Authority of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement and, in any event, submit each required novation, recognition, change-of-control, or similar request no later than ten (10) Business Days after the date of this Agreement, or such earlier date as required by applicable Law or contract.\

> (b) Seller and the Company shall prepare and submit complete request packages, including the information required under FAR §42.1204 and analogous state requirements, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all required novation agreements, recognition agreements, consents, or written confirmations that interim performance may continue. Seller shall provide Buyer drafts before submission and copies of all submissions, responses, and communications promptly after delivery or receipt.\

> (c) From the date of this Agreement through the Closing, Seller shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, withdraw, amend, or materially supplement any submission without Buyer's prior written consent. Following the Closing, Seller shall continue to provide reasonable cooperation, information, signatures, and participation in meetings requested by Buyer in connection with any pending novation or recognition process for at least twelve (12) months.\
> Add the following to Section 7.02 as a new clause (h):\

> (h) Government Contract Status. With respect to each Government Contract for which a novation, recognition, consent, or change-of-control submission is required, (i) the required submission has been made, (ii) the applicable contracting officer has not denied the request or indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, or materially modify the Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, and (iii) Buyer has received written confirmation that interim performance may continue pending final action, if a final novation or recognition agreement has not been executed. Buyer may waive this condition in writing.

> **TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** This is a critical risk allocation issue. The DD memo states that the federal contracts may require novation under FAR §42.1204 and that failure to obtain required novation could result in termination. Given agency timing, the recommended interim position is not to require executed novations as an absolute closing condition; instead require submission of all packages, no denial or termination signal, and written confirmation that interim performance may continue, with a post-closing cooperation tail. Elena should discuss with Marcus whether to push for executed novations as a hard condition or retain this balanced formulation. See DD Memo §§VI.B--C, Buyer Playbook §12.2 and §13.2(a), and Partner Instructions ¶4.
# Article VI --- Covenants
## **4. Interim affiliate-transaction restriction**
**PRIORITY: HIGH \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §6.01(b); Seller SPA §§4.21, Schedule 4.09, Schedule 4.21; Buyer Playbook §3.2; Partner Instructions ¶8*

**Issue summary.** The interim covenant lists general restrictions but omits an express prohibition on new, amended, extended, renewed, terminated, or paid affiliate transactions. This is material because the Company pays \$1,600,000 annual rent under the Seller-affiliate lease and has disclosed a \$350,000 annual management-services arrangement. Those arrangements can be expanded or accelerated between signing and closing unless expressly restricted.
**Original seller language.**

> **SELLER DRAFT ---** Section 6.01(b) prohibits specified actions, including amendments to material contracts, but contains no specific restriction on transactions with Seller, Seller affiliates, or Seller-related persons. Section 4.21 merely discloses existing affiliate transactions.
**Draft-ready buyer language.**
> **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** Add the following as a new clause (xiv) to Section 6.01(b):\

> (xiv) directly or indirectly (A) enter into any Contract, transaction, or arrangement with Seller, any Affiliate of Seller, or any officer, director, manager, member, shareholder, partner, or family member of Seller or any Affiliate of Seller, (B) amend, modify, extend, renew, supplement, or otherwise alter any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with any such Person, (C) make any payment or transfer any asset to any such Person, other than compensation payments to employees in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice, or (D) terminate any existing Contract, transaction, or arrangement with any such Person, in each case without Buyer's prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

> **TRACK-CHANGES COMMENT.** The covenant follows the playbook's mandatory affiliate-transaction formulation and directly addresses the above-market rent adjustment identified in the quality-of-earnings materials and the Seller-affiliate lease disclosed in Schedule 4.09. Disclosure alone does not prevent value leakage during the interim period. See Buyer Playbook §3.2 and Partner Instructions ¶8.
## **5. Closing indebtedness --- payoff letters and simultaneous funds-flow repayment**
**PRIORITY: HIGH \| Sources:** *Seller SPA §§2.03(d), 7.02; Term Sheet §6; Buyer Playbook §9.2; Partner Instructions ¶9*

**Issue summary.** The draft permits repayment "at or promptly following" closing and provides no payoff-letter condition. That is inconsistent with the term sheet and will not satisfy Clearwater Environmental Lending Corp.'s funding and lien-release requirements. The three identified holders are Cascade Mutual Bank (\$28,000,000), Pacific Lease Corp. (\$9,800,000), and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. (\$4,500,000).
**Original seller language.**

> **SELLER DRAFT ---** "At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness." The Buyer closing conditions contain no express payoff-letter delivery condition.
**Draft-ready buyer language.**
> **BUYER PROPOSED REPLACEMENT ---** Replace Section 2.03(d) with the following:\

> (d) Payoff Letters; Simultaneous Repayment. Seller shall deliver to Buyer, or cause to be delivered, executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness, including Cascade Mutual Bank, Pacific Lease Corp., and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc., no later than three (3) Business Days before the Closing Date. Each payoff letter shall state the total amount required to repay the applicable obligation in full as of the Closing Date, including principal, accrued interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, fees, and other amounts; provide wiring instructions; and provide for the prompt release of all liens and other Encumbrances securing the obligation, including delivery of UCC termination statements and other lien-release documents.
